review.Pros: The communication is very good and they actually listen to my complaints. If something is wrong they work to rectify it rather than ignoring it or basically not helping.
review.Cons: The main con I have is that there is no employee matching. Because of how I am classified I basically am an employee with benefits but not that specific benefit. Others in the company have it but employees with my designation don't
review.Advice to management: Keep supporting your employees

review.Pros: The pay is pretty good and the benefits used to be good. I can set my own schedule and I like working with patients, so that is one big Pro.
review.Cons: BEnefits are pretty bad now, they took away a lot of health coverage. We don't get raises at the rate we should get raises. I wish we had more money for continuing education.
review.Advice to management: Invest in your people more so that they want to stick around. We are health professionals, so it's not like we don't have other options.

review.Pros: The office is well located in a nice neighborhood and has plenty of parking available. My colleagues are helpful and friendly, so the working conditions are very good.
review.Cons: The computer equipment and printer available at the office are a bit out of date.  The manager does not spend much money on advertising, so our name recognition could be better.
review.Advice to management: Update the computers and the printer. Spend more on advertising the business.

review.Pros: I think some of the pros are having such a laid back boss. He takes care of us and pays us well.  He understands what the normal people go through and makes sure we are happy!
review.Cons: Getting paid once a month can be tough. Also even though you can be on the clock sometimes you aren't very productive depending on what the job requires.
review.Advice to management: Try and make sure materials are readily available so there is less downtime.

review.Pros: My direct management is supportive and receptive. I am able to grow my strengths and incorporate them into my work in an enjoyable way that supports students.
review.Cons: There is not much room for growth. When you are the only one doing your job, there is no way up. It is just me.

review.Pros: Health insurance costs are relatively low, good coworkers, normal 8-5 work hours with weekends off, ability to retire with state benefits after 28 years of service.
review.Cons: No chances of moving up the ladder, little direction from management, low pay that never increases, management doesn't know what they are doing, no training opportunities.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your employees for once.

review.Pros: There is some flexibility in shifts and the guests are generally good natured and want to have a good time. The work itself is pretty easy and not to demanding.
review.Cons: There is often significant understaffing which makes the job more stressful. You may end up doing multiple jobs to help cover other departments. You do not always have all of the equipment needed to get your job done correctly.
review.Advice to management: Try to staff correctly and your employees will be happier.

review.Pros: There are decent employee benefits and you get very familiar with the merchaniside, which comes in handy furing the holiday season. We do do a couple of promos or deals throughout the year which is pretty fun. You get alot of interactions with sweet people with similar hobbies, which is a 10/10 experience.
review.Cons: They change a lot  of stuff often, so its hard when it comes to keeping track of info- theyre also not super consistent with some of their rules. You do also get a lot of entitled people, which isnt great to deal with but thats par for any retail job.

review.Pros: Has great benefits, and work life balance.  They really try to keep it family oriented and give you flex ability with work hours and allow remote work.
review.Cons: The biggest con is the pay. You can definitely find better salaries other place.  The locations of buildings are off high ways but in very expense areas to live so most work outside those areas.  But they are also high traffic areas so the commute stinks.  C levels in my opinion are still trying to figure out since the original C levels left.
review.Advice to management: Continue to involved take employees suggestions to heart.

review.Pros: The pay is good.  Better then I can get at a private company. I get a lot of holidays off. They are very felixble with time off.
review.Cons: Management is not firm on what they say. They speak out of both sides of their mouth. They don't seem to care about their employees.
review.Advice to management: Get a backbone and stand up for people.

review.Pros: Stady work, most employees get along and I have made true friends. My location is close to home, not far to travel. The health benifits are good
review.Cons: The pay is not the beat, we have bot gotten any kind of raises in over 3 years. It is very dirty and can be unsafe at timees
review.Advice to management: Give at least a cost of living increase and value your employees

review.Pros: It's okay, the work is fairly reasonable and the culture is decent, at least it's fairly friendly LGBT-wise, but I feel stifled there and feel I need to move on to something different. It's no longer working for me anymore.
review.Cons: I don't like how my work tasks are the same and I don't have much challenge or room to grow. It feels like I'm not accomplishing much of note and I feel like I need to get a different job in maybe even a new field. Like I can do the work but I just don't have the drive anymore.

review.Pros: USPS is one of the last jobs you can get off the street with no education in which you can get a 401k equivalent, health insurance, and a pension.
review.Cons: Management does everything they can to fire you, as you cost more money the longer you work there.  There is a hostile work environment at all times.  Crimes are covered up.
review.Advice to management: Clean house.  Get rid of most local management across the country

review.Pros: Corewell Health offers a great PTO package. I started off with 4 weeks and one 1 day right upon hire. Additionally, they have a decent sick package which we can use whenever as long as we have the PTO. My pay has increased over $5 since I was first hired two years ago. There are other departments within the company that you can transfer to, so, room for growth is easy.
review.Cons: There is lots of gossip in between the departments. Management does not really do anything about employees that are late on a daily basis. The rewards for your yearly anniversary are pretty dismal. They do require every other holidays and weekends for some roles.
review.Advice to management: I have no negative advice for my direct management. I think they're all great at their jobs.

review.Pros: It is a relatively stable place to work. As long as you do your job competently, you generally do not have to worry about losing it.
review.Cons: They tend to be understaffed and underpaid across pretty much all divisions. They hold a bit of a monopoly in the area so there isn't much competition.

review.Pros: Great worker benefits that can be used and depended on, every day is a new learning experience. Flexible work arrangements and scheduling. Multiple extra groups to participate and learn from.
review.Cons: Limited trainings for new tools and processes. Holidays are required to be worked. Organizational changes very often. Limited promotional opportunities. Lot of self learning and experiences.
review.Advice to management: Be more involved with the teams you are working for. Listen to them when they are reaching their wits end.

review.Pros: First are solid benefits, for medical coverage, and PTO which is above the average most companies give. Another is having good professionally support and autonomy at a majority of the staff are allowed to work fully remotely here in the US.
review.Cons: You are subjected to the risk of being employed at a large corporate company which does not mean you have automatic job security. You have to put your whole effort into your work, and not take it for granted in the slightest.
review.Advice to management: Don't take your hard workers for granted.

review.Pros: There are several pros of working at IRG. The main perk is that they offer competitive salaries as well as in addition to good continuing education benefits.
review.Cons: One of the cons is that, for some reason, some of the most incompetent people are those in management positions. I really don't know how most managers/directors got where they are.
review.Advice to management: Try to be more competent.

review.Pros: Pros include stability, as LECOM Health is constantly growing. The health benefits are really good if you use their providers. The match on the 403(b) is 6%.
review.Cons: They can be a little in their own world sometimes. Not always the most gracious or thankful for their employees. Always want more and will highlight mistakes over milestones.
review.Advice to management: Invest in your people and prop them up whenever you can.

review.Pros: working from home 100% of the time, insurance benefits, trust and confidence from leadership to mostly accomplish my tasks without much oversight. pto accumulation is decent
review.Cons: terrible communication from upper management, lack of support from upper management, decisions made without the interest of employees and members. us vs them mentality is prevelant across different teams
review.Advice to management: listen to employee feedback, stop making decisions with profits in mind

review.Pros: The main pros would probably be the prestige associated and relatedly the size of the clients. Working on major deals and cases is beneficial to my career (both currently and for future prospects). The pay is also solid, there is good training, and the people are great (both personally and in terms of things like diverse backgrounds).
review.Cons: The main cons would be that the hours are not the best (and can be brutal at times). It is a pretty competitive environment, so there is lots of pressures to bill and prove yourself constantly. As a result, the work-life balance is not completely commensurate with my ideal and so the stress can also be pretty intense. But I've found this is generally true of a lot of firms so I'm unsure how directly attributable it is to my organization.
review.Advice to management: Though the training is good, I think mentoring junior staff members a bit more instead of throwing work at them without much clear guidance would be helpful. Also cutting back on unrealistic workloads. Also the environment is currently good for this to a degree, but creating more of a culture where people actually talk about struggles they are facing versus venting behind closed doors would be helpful.

review.Pros: The pay and benefits are generally good.  Retirement is excellent, with both employer matching 401k and a pension.  Plenty of opportunity for advancement/promotion.  Job security is fairly decent, though it can depend on who is in charge.
review.Cons: All of the cons that come with military/federal government work.  Whoever gets elected has a lot of influence on things like job security and pay and if they aren't supportive, things will get bad.  Manning is also extremely low which means extra work for everyone.

review.Pros: Excellent coworkers and it is giving me the experience that I need to apply for school. It is also close to my house which makes it easy for me.
review.Cons: Our pay rate is abysmal and we get extremely small raises every year. The protocols in place are outdated and need to be replaced. We float too much.
review.Advice to management: Pay your staff what they're worth.

review.Pros: This is a remote first company which is important to me.  I have significant autonomy and the benefits are good as well as my schedule.
review.Cons: The company is embracing technical trends like AI without enough foresight.  In additiona, layoffs are regular and do not take into account the institutional knowledge lost.

review.Pros: Working at Delta means you'll be on a hybrid schedule with only two days required per month in the office, but it will be bumped up to one day a week. The benefits are decent and the office itself is nice.
review.Cons: Management is incompetent and the salaries are low for the amount of work you are asked to do. They are investing heavily into AI and are using it to determine which jobs can be cut going forward.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your subordinates, actually implement solutions that address the constant negative feedback the company receives on surveys, and improve the work-life balance for all employees by hiring more heads.

review.Pros: The flexibility of the shifts and work schedule where you can choose your own schedule, the ease of the work, and the relaxed feel to each day
review.Cons: Our owner is very pro-AI and that causes some situations to arise where things are done in an uncohesive manner because his decision-making was only dependent on the AI. There are also times where his decisions hurt the business rather than help it.
review.Advice to management: Do not rely so much on the AI to drive business decisions, give more faith and trust to your employees.

review.Pros: They are a big company so they have decent benefits like retirement and health insurance. They also have discounts with other companies and shopping places.
review.Cons: Since they are a big global company, it makes it hard to stand out in the workplace. You feel like you are just a number.

review.Pros: it is a very nice facility, most residents and employees are very friendly!  We have the supplies and resources necessary to complete our job.  There is always help available when needed!
review.Cons: Our healthcare insurance is very expensive.  It can be so busy that is almost feels impossible to get everything that needs to be done, done at times
review.Advice to management: Step in and help out more, even if you don't typically do that specific job duty.  Of course stay within scope of practice!

review.Pros: The company makes you feel listened to and like they truly care about your thoughts and opinions in dealing with the company before changes are made
review.Cons: I feel obligated to work overtime when they ask because of the way they are always taking care of me and the other employees with the company
review.Advice to management: na

review.Pros: The work is meaningful, you can adjust your schedule very easily, you are treated as a human and are not shamed when life events occur and may interrupt your schedule and/or performance.
review.Cons: The pay you receive is not equal to the amount of work you'll put in, the days can be challenging, and training is very limited.
review.Advice to management: Even if basic, please provide your employees with the tools you would like them to use such as trauma-informed care practices - or what trauma-informed care looks like.

review.Pros: Pros, works with children with disabilities giving them the chance to be successful in a school enviorment. Cons, not enough professionals for the classrooms but a strain on others.
review.Cons: Cons, helping children with disabilities learn social, behavior and job skill so they can be successful in getting a job and maintaining a job with as little supports as necessary
review.Advice to management: Keep doing what they are doing it works. Try to find creative ways to get more educators.

review.Pros: All team members work remotely and have autonomy to work when they prefer as long as deadlines are met. Company is extremely family oriented and very encouraging in work-life balance.
review.Cons: The owners of the company are elderly, and sometimes forget to pass along information, or they don't see the best and most efficient ways of making progress.
review.Advice to management: You have hired an excellent staff; listen to their input and implement it.

review.Pros: the friends i have made along the way make the excruciating never ending pedal to the metal grind somewhat bearable.if it wasnt for my coworker/friends i would have left long ago.
review.Cons: it is like slave labor. they barely pay anything but expect you to hustle from the time you clock in till you go home. and dont ask for a raise because it aint happening.if there was any other viable option open at night i would leave in a heartbeat.
review.Advice to management: treat people like human beings and pay them a living wage.if the CEO can have a 8 figure salary then i shouldnt need foodstamps to survive.and one more thing...turn the darn air conditioning ON!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

review.Pros: It depends on the post assigned, but at mine I have a great post, great supervisor, great coworkers.  Weekly pay.  App for easily tracking paychecks and schedules.  Good pay rate at my site.
review.Cons: The initial AI interview was ridiculously stupid, a redundant waste of time.  The occasional pay mistake that takes weeks to correct.  Too many coworkers calling off.
review.Advice to management: Stop the AI interview crap, just let us get prescreened by a human, it worked for decades prior.

review.Pros: The pros include great coworkers who are passionate about their jobs, a fantastic supervisor, and a good amount of paid holidays and days off. I also get to experience fun events for free while working them.
review.Cons: Navigating the Jesuit background can be difficult. I also do not get paid well, especially for the amount of emotional labor I do on top of my actual tasks.

review.Pros: Great competitive pay, flexible working opportunities, interesting subject matter, receptive management, close location to me, generous PTO allocation, in the beginning, a lot of opportunities to move up.
review.Cons: No room for growth after you reach a certain point, both in opportunities and pay. No extra training opportunities. Human resources department leaves a little to be desired.
review.Advice to management: Consider not only attorney's opinions, but staff as well.

review.Pros: Autonomous decision making and problem solving is the norm. Creative exploration is encouraged. The ends justify the means provided there is a positive end outcome.
review.Cons: Budget restrictions are a stronghold to fluid brainstorming. Rate limits are dictated from outside and are never announced in advance, so there are constant interruptions.
review.Advice to management: Go for the VC offerings.

review.Pros: The pros of working for Amazon is that they do provide decent benefits and time off options. They pay decent for what it is, they should still pay more. Meeting new people.
review.Cons: The cons of working for Amazon is that the work can be tiring and redundant. There are work place politics that can be toxic. Working with crazy people. They have somewhat strict and inconsistent policies.

review.Pros: The pros depend on your profession.  The university employs professors and I don't know their working conditions.  There a many support staff such as office assistants.  There are health benefits and paid vacation.  The university will close for at least a week in december, so there is more paid time off than in most other professions.  The work area is cleaned regularly and is a nice place.
review.Cons: University budget can be affected by government grants.  If the economy is bad then one can expect layoffs.  Education systems are financially bloated and if people decide that higher education is too expensive for what you receive, then the work situation will get worse.  Support staff are not paid a lot, but if your job is stable then it can last until you decide to move on to other things.

review.Pros: Good fellow workers, work at your own pace, company truck. Eating meetings minimum once a month. Boots and t-shirts are made available to us all.
review.Cons: Hot days, rainy days, cold weather, bad traffic...it all makes your day longer. Midnight call outs for down signs is definitely not a plus to me.

review.Pros: The give excellent pay. All holidays we are closed. Quickly you earn person time off as well as vacation days. Everyone is treated like family.
review.Cons: At my company we do not have any cons that honestly come to my mind and I have worked here for many years and plan to stay here
review.Advice to management: Keep up the excellent work

review.Pros: I am able to work flexible hours and from home or in the office. I kept up-to-date on all of the advancements in computers and technology.
review.Cons: I have to follow a strict set of rules. If anything I do is in a grey area, I could lose my job. I have to always learn about the newest technologies as soon as possible, or else I might lose my job.
review.Advice to management: Use actual humans for support and not AI bots. They are too generic to help fix anything.

review.Pros: The benefits of working here are quite good and include a good health insurance plan, flexible time off, children tuition benefits, generous holidays off, and overall good work life balance. There is also quite a bit of prestige working for this organization in the community.
review.Cons: There is a big emphasis on hierarchy, so it can be hard to get things accomplished unless you are in senior leadership. Things also rely on reputations and who-you-know, so sometimes it can feel not genuine or forced when interacting with people. Some people are also rewarded just because of reputation/connections rather than actual hard work or output.
review.Advice to management: Be more consistent in evaluation of employees; correctly identify top performers and reward them instead of those who aren't actually performing and are just well-liked/well-connected

review.Pros: Unlimited PTO, Flex-time, Paid Holidays, Not a micromanaging environment, work from home options and flexibility around it. Incentives with new business help increase pay too!
review.Cons: Upper Management truly has no idea what is going on. Corporate makes a lot of promises and never delivers on it which is very frustrating.
review.Advice to management: Go back to how mom and pop agencies are ran. They were successful for a reason.

review.Pros: Insight is a very large company with a large footprint in the IT services and MSP space. It has allowed me to work with several different teams, software, and projects over the years. I have control of my own career and can pivot to something new if I get bored or see an opportunity to move forward with my career.
review.Cons: Insight is a very big, public company that has a lot of executives. They are very profit driven. They, unfortunately, do not hesitate to layoff employees whenever they want to improve 'profits' or their own bonus checks.
review.Advice to management: Lower management cares about their teams and helps them be successful. Upper management could take a hint and work like them and not just profit.

review.Pros: They offer health insurance from day one and offer other good benefits. They have a strong 401k match and tuition reimbursement. They actively promote from within and offer employees opportunities for growth.
review.Cons: During winter months, it can be very busy and there can be a lot of over time. You are expected to work all holidays and will not have them off.

review.Pros: One pro of working at Nike is the discount that employees receive (40% off). Another pro of working at this company is that there are opportunities to experience how certain events are rolled out in partnership with other organizations (i.e. NBA All-Star Weekend, NFL Super Bowl, World Cup).
review.Cons: One con of working at Nike is the toxic work environment between middle management and corporate and the retail front. Another con is that there is no work-life balance. A third con is that there is no room for professional development. A fourth con is that the onboarding of individuals who have a higher title is terrible, especially if they are not part of the Nike ecosystem.
review.Advice to management: Consistent communication/message across all levels that lay out the expectations of employees.

review.Pros: Besides the security of a state job.  The organization has an excellent pension, generous health benefits and a unique workplace away from the main city of state government.  There is a large freedom of operation and management is supportive of staff development and family needs.
review.Cons: Pay is somewhat lower than in the private sector.  Limited opportunities to move within the agency as it is small, but entire state is open for promotions and moves.
review.Advice to management: Continue to provide support for employees, make reasonable expectations and continue to operate at a high professional level.

review.Pros: I have a remote position with a flexible work schedule. I work with clients from the disabled community providing mobility equipment and support in terms of claims.
review.Cons: Extremely complicated insurance/ payer issues dealing with getting claims paid by insurance carriers that are repeatedly stressful. Continued issues in the healthcare industry specific to insurance.

review.Pros: It has a very family oriented environment. We support each other and everyone wants the team to succeed. Its a booming business that I'm happy to be apart of.
review.Cons: Maybe the salary. If I had to pick one thing it would be wanting to be paid more but overall I can't pick anything else out.
review.Advice to management: n/a

review.Pros: The money is extremely good in season. I make anywhere from $50/hr to $100/hr depending on if we are in or out of season. I work with a lot of great people and the company provides health insurance.
review.Cons: Management treats employees like they are disposable and recently have fired many great employees over trivial things. You will always feel like you are walking on eggshells.
review.Advice to management: Realize that even the most seasoned servers and bartenders will make mistakes on occasion. Of course it is important how they handle those mistakes, but they should be allowed grace from time to time.

review.Pros: The Pros of working at LA Fitness are: base pay + commission, long breaks, being able to work inside a gym, the clientele, and the ability to impact people in a positive way.
review.Cons: The cons of working at LA Fitness: the long breaks, poor management, slow sales, poor structure, and the long drive. I also dislike how low the base pay is and how annoying the selling aspect is.
review.Advice to management: Train employees better.

review.Pros: Working at Walmart has provided a good opportunity to develop customer service, teamwork, and problem solving skills. The store offers a variety of departments and opportunities to learn new opportunities - when one area isn't a good fit for you, you're encouraged to try someplace different until you find a place that's mutually beneficial. Coworkers and management are more often than not supportive, and the opportunities to grow and advance within the company are plentiful... if you're truly committed and put in the effort.. The benefits are surprisingly good, especially now that the employee discount covers almost everything (I've literally saved hundreds on my groceries). Work environment can be a bit overwhelming and fast pace, but once you get used to it the time flies and it's worth it.
review.Cons: The fast paced environment and physical demands can often be extremely exhausting mentally and physically especially around the end of the year holidays. Staffing levels can make it difficult to keep up with everything as we're constantly understaffed in every department. This results in tasks being delayed, neglected, or pushed to other shifts unfairly adding to their already heavy load. Communication between management and associates could be more consistent. It's not uncommon for one team lead to say one thing, another to tell you to do something else, then their boss/our coach say something completely different or the priorities conflict with the finite staff and time resources available.
review.Advice to management: Continue improving communication and consistency across departments. Clear expectations, regular feedback, and recognition for associates who go above and beyond can help improve morale, teamwork, and overall productivity.

review.Pros: we have good benefits. the job has a better than average value. we have excellent time off.  for the most part it is a positive atmosphere
review.Cons: the job can require extreme patience and very high responsibility rate. it can be emotionally draining at times. the pay is not the best in our area

review.Pros: Great team environment, positive opportunities for growth and good benefits offered. Able to take part in retirement fund to save and plan for the future
review.Cons: Lack of opportunities for promotions, low raises, fear of losing job. Not thr best management that does not care about employees especially higher up management

review.Pros: Flexible shift and scheduling. Good pay.  Great staff and work environment. We do a great job and serving our community with excellent patient care in a compassionate setting
review.Cons: We often work weekends and Holidays without a shift differential.  Paid time off is only 2 weeks and there a minimal other benefits such as health care

review.Pros: Great work life balance, the people there are very friendly and helpful. The benefits are good as we have good health insurance and a good 401k plan.
review.Cons: The bonus and compensation structure isn't always fair. Sometimes you are overlooked for a raise or promotion even if you do outstanding work. The people at the top of the organization are in charge and making these decisions so they don't even know you.

review.Pros: The primary mission of AABCP is to educate and advocate breast care professionals across the globe. This is an extraordinary environment in which to work; knowing you are helping people,
review.Cons: It can be frustrating as events and business focus are constantly in flux. Because it is an NGO-Professional Association, funding depends on grants, memeberships, and professional support.
review.Advice to management: Engage supporters and employees to understand the ever evolving professional environment.

review.Pros: The firm does a lot of business with a number of large well established firms, so there are various opportunities to get involved with some work for the company.
review.Cons: The company and CEO are essentially broke and have had to cut a large portion of the staff to try to cut losses, however there has been a vast increase in the number of clients and the amount of business they do, so this is difficult for the reduced staff to manage.
review.Advice to management: Hire people or at least stop cutting people, otherwise the service will continue to suffer.

review.Pros: It is a small-ish company so it's pretty easy to get to know people and how to do things. It is also pretty flexible and the helps with work/life balance.
review.Cons: Lack of advancement oppourtunities. The pay is not great. There is not a lot of formal training. There is not a lot of things that might otherwise be at other companies, other perks.

review.Pros: Having 24 hour shifts as an EMT, Electric stair chairs, and people who sort of care about you working around you. The benefits are pretty okay as well.
review.Cons: I've been injured multiple times due to the incompetence and failure to plan of the members of my team, and due to the problems fomented by bad management. We often loose vital sleep for unnsessecary transports.
review.Advice to management: You need to clear house of your supervisory teams.

review.Pros: I love working with the kids, and the community is great. I also love my coworkers. The school I work at has a great great admin team who supports my work.
review.Cons: We do not get paid well for the degrees they require us to have. The pay does not match the cost of living in the area.
review.Advice to management: none

review.Pros: Cox has good benefits that it works to ensure all employees are aware of and have access to. Frequent communication from upper management in attempts to bring transparency to all levels. Most departments are flexible-ish with circumstances like work hours, remote work, etc.
review.Cons: No realistic work-life balance. Constantly insists on doing more with less. Frequent restructuring with little concern on employee impact. No budget for raises - does not even match cost of living.

review.Pros: There are a variety of professionals working at NYU. There are many disciplines and schools. For example there is the washington square campus, the school of nursing, dentistry, and medicine.
review.Cons: The campus is spread across the city. It is not always easy to get to one class from another. People can be siloed depending on their major or discipline.
review.Advice to management: Consider that student are paying a very high tuition and should be accomodated, but at the same time students don't always know what they need.

review.Pros: The company is small and family oriented. Everyone works together to support each other because everyone works together on all projects. The job is mostly work from home, with some travel.
review.Cons: Since the company is so small, everyone has their hand in everyone's work. That means that you will often have to assist on projects or issues that are not yours originally. Travel can be hard if you have a family.
review.Advice to management: Give people some better guidance on responsibilities.

review.Pros: The work is remote and you are provided with a computer, monitor, mouse, keyboard, and mouse. There are also decent bonuses if you meet your goal.
review.Cons: Very low pay, the annual raise is incredibly low and doesn't take into account cost of living, every week you are given so many stupid tasks that take away from your main job, the company also doesn't care to provide the right resources for you to do your job in a timely manor.

review.Pros: free insurance, working with a great team that I get to work at, summers off, winter break, pto used as needed, provided continuing education for licensure
review.Cons: There is low pay, currently on a hiring freeze, no approved steps or salary increase, current investigations, not provided with materials, low morale from workers

review.Pros: I like interacting with customers and being part of a growing industry. I learn a lot working here from my peers and supervisors, and help me see a future in this industry.
review.Cons: It can be a lot of work sometimes between dealing wikth customers, taking deliveries and making sure we are staying compliant with state regulations and guidelines

review.Pros: I like the repetitive tasks as well as how it is a surprisingly interesting place to work at, but it is not too chaotic to be stressful.
review.Cons: Sometimes working with the public can be a big challenge, and people are often gross or unhygienic  with items that we have to deal with regularly.

review.Pros: There are so many resources and good causes that are being worked towards. The comapny is working to do good, is prestigious, and has moral leadership.
review.Cons: The severe underpaying of certain employees, especially becuase they have a prestigious title, they are able to pay less than other places might. There are also so many employees that one person is easily lost.

review.Pros: make your own hours, earn as much as you want, no earning caps, cash out at your own descretion,  pick what type of clients you want to work for
review.Cons: very little constructive feedback on your work, you can get kicked off the platform at any time for any reason without a heads-up, a warning, or explanation

review.Pros: God accrual of paid time off, good benefits, I like all my coworkers and my supervisors, the work load is not too demanding and the agency encourages staff building
review.Cons: There is a large amount of employees that work for the agency so it is not always possible to meet and get to know everyone
review.Advice to management: N/A

review.Pros: The pros are that it is completely remote and has a flexible schedule. The benefits are amazing, and they implement many policies that are staff-centered.
review.Cons: One con is that because the organization is entirely remote, you don't have the ability to have meaningful connections with your coworkers. Your interaction are limited to zoom meetings.
review.Advice to management: no

review.Pros: I have freedom to perform my work in the way I choose, I can work at home a couple of days a week, my boss and coworkers are great to work with.
review.Cons: The place is run by a Trump sycophant and anyone who expresses disagreement with her racism and sexism is fired on the spot. This can be avoided by keeping your head down and your mouth shut.

review.Pros: I am 100 percent work from home, I do have to work 8-5 but I have flexability on how and I work and in what order, I also have felxability to adjust my hours as need be for family commitments.
review.Cons: Our company offers no insurance of any kind, no medical, no dental, no flexible spending account, nor are we paid enough to get something from the marketplace, but we all earn too much to qualify for any kind of state aid like medicade
review.Advice to management: Get more clients and give us medical benefits.

review.Pros: ERG is a company that values it's employees.  It prioritizes diversity and inclusivity. The company provides great benefits and also allows for work life balance.
review.Cons: I am a remote employee so I don't experience many of the day-to-day cons of being in an office. I truly don't have any negative words about the company.
review.Advice to management: No notes.

review.Pros: The coworkers are easily some of the easiest people to work with. Everybody loves the plant, is happy to chat, and is easy to get along with. Everyone is their to do their job and most of the time do it well.
review.Cons: The company has rare chances for upward movement, rarely wants to pay for anything, and does not pay its employees what their labor is worth. Oftentimes you will drown with minimal support, and give way more effort and personal assets than should be necessary.
review.Advice to management: Understand that your employees are overworked, underpaid, and fed up. Offer help and speak up to higher ups.

review.Pros: Great coworkers that are great at team work. Helpful and understanding supervisors that step in to help if needed. Great ability to advance your career
review.Cons: Sometimes you are short staffed which cause stress and having to work double shift. Long hours and sometimes more work than you can get done in a shift
review.Advice to management: Keep staffing at optimal levels

review.Pros: We are the largest school district in our state.  Yet, we are still able to see thousands of successful students living enriching lives when they graduate.  It is easier to have a small district where you have success, but to have such a large district with over 180,000 students, we still are student focused which is what I love the most
review.Cons: The biggest con is that we do get a lot of students who are underprivileged, and it can be very challenging to get them up to speed.  We do not have the most affluent students in my school, so we do our best to help them achievve

review.Pros: The upper management is very understanding and feels like you work for a family run business.  Some of the people that I work with have been there for over 40 years.  They allow very flexible work schedules for the people at my level.
review.Cons: It is a fast food restaurant owner, so the working conditions can be very hectic and hard at times.  Tough working with both difficult customers and difficult team members.  Somedays I feel like I am running an adult daycare.
review.Advice to management: Be ready for something new to hit you everyday and be prepared to work hard and you have to be able to think on your feet .

review.Pros: Excellent benefits. Good healthcare, wellness plan, an awesome HSA program. Lots of extra options for additional coverage. Descent pay per hour. Bosses are descent. Remote working locations.
review.Cons: Customer base for the company is horrible. Customer's are a technical support persons nightmare. Raises are very minimal. Stats are hard to achieve. Make suggestions, but they rarely get added.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your employees.

review.Pros: Reakky good work life balance, considerate leadership team and great benefits ( insurance, and vacation time). I really feel like my work has a positive impact on the team and I feel very supported
review.Cons: To be honest, I can not say so much. one slight challenge I face is because I work in a cross functional role, there are a lot of stakeholders I work with and it could get confusing

review.Pros: Independence in how I can accomplish my work and tasks, high pay, the ability to work remotely. I also value the competitive benefit package, including unlimited PTO and a good 401k match.
review.Cons: Unclear org structure and vision. At times "decisions" are not enforced or given enough time to be seen through because of rapidly changing leadership and hesitance to interrupt business operations.
review.Advice to management: More transparent decision making, with clear timelines. i.e, "If we are doing X, we will revisit the decision in 5 years to see how it did"

review.Pros: A cultural and values match with compassionate capitalism & underserved neighborhood revitalization.  The chance to make an impact om entire families, therefor on entire communities and doing something that makes a difference!
review.Cons:
Typical growing organization growing pains.  Making the switch to corporate style knowledge and structure instead of a loose organization where everyone is a subject matter expert and keeper of the knowledge for their part of the company with no guidelines.  
You must be flexible and willing to pivot as necessary.
review.Advice to management: Speed up the SOP and guidelines part.  We can keep up with the pace we have, IF we have guidelines in place and a way to get answers that don't rely on anyone else, but I know it's a work in progress too.

review.Pros: I have job security, decent health insurance, a lot of time off, good work/life balance, and a sense of purpose to do my job and help my fellow citizens.
review.Cons: Leadership changes a lot based on the administration in office and we have to follow the rules even if they don't make sense. (Return to Office). Also, not much opportunity to increase your paycheck besides the regularly scheduled promotions or step increases.
review.Advice to management: Delegate down to supervisors who should actual know and manage their employees. Train your supervisors so they manage properly.

review.Pros: Best company I've ever worked for. Great culture that starts at the top. I plan to finish my career here. There's fair pay, great treatment, and chances to grow.
review.Cons: I honestly can't think of many cons. I guess one is the location. We're on the east coast in a town that isn't necessarily desirable. This makes it hard to attract talent from around the country.
review.Advice to management: Keep doing what you're doing. Avoid going "woke" please. Just focus on being the best you can at what you do, and don't get involved or outspoken about social issues.

review.Pros: A highly engaged owner who takes a great deal of interest in the lives of his employees. A fair amount of autonomy and freedom, as well as interesting and intellectually engaging work.
review.Cons: Owner can be unreasonable in his expectations of employees, the pay is horribly low, owner and management have no concept of work-life balance. Work can also sometimes be ethically questionable.
review.Advice to management: Learn ethics and proper management.

review.Pros: The community at the workplace is welcoming and helpful, making you feel like part of the team.  You can find a place here and people who will support you.
review.Cons: The push for monthly goals can make you feel as if your work doesn't matter.  The recent need for more overtime to make these goals is hard on morale.
review.Advice to management: Layout a process for goals that makes it seem like there is a real plan for workers to follow.

review.Pros: The pros are that it affords me an excellent work-life schedule. I enjoy that I am not micro managed. I also enjoy that i am able to make my own decisions
review.Cons: The only con that I have is that it is so far away. The traffic in the area can get pretty bad during major events.
review.Advice to management: Make sure you are an example to your team.

review.Pros: The pros of working at EXCM are generous health insurance, 401k match and that it is a non-profit. I work with a very supportive group of people.
review.Cons: The cons of working at ECXM are lower pay than average for my role. While they offer many PTO days, we do not get many holidays off and have to schedule back-up coverage for all PTO. I also have to use my personal vehicle.
review.Advice to management: Please consider that the wage is lower than average for this role as well as employees have to use their own vehicles for work. The wear and tear on the vehicle is very expensive in this economy. This paired with the lower than average wage likely adds to the high turnover rate.

review.Pros: The company is committed to its mission of making high quality products and there is a good amount of innovation. In general most employees are supportive of one another.
review.Cons: The company offers decent pay but there is room for improvement. Management can at times offer confusing directives. Training for some important skills could be done better.

review.Pros: They are not going out of business anytime. Solid company to work with and they have been around for the longest. Good pay and benefits
review.Cons: Too many over worked the hours are never the same. Constant rescturing of management and changing policies this is retail and you have to know what your getting into.
review.Advice to management: Be fair and consistent

review.Pros: It is fairly flexible and the position/nature of the work interests me a lot. It is really relevant to my career aspirations, which looks good on my resume. The founder who I work for is fairly understandable.
review.Cons: It is a startup, so the scale of things is small. For example, we are not deploying production-grade systems but are more so experimenting. Also, it is a startup and an internship so the pay isn't a lot.

review.Pros: Kind coworkers, rooms for advancement, flexibility, and there is not too much stress or any negative workplace issues. The pay meets my needs for the most part and I like all that I work with.
review.Cons: Sometimes the phone rings back to back and it can be difficult to keep up. That and I believe every company struggles with communication to some degree.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Airbus is that you never get the opportunity to be bored.  It is an everchanging environment that keeps you on your toes.
review.Cons: The cons is that there is more management than workers.  We spend most of our days in meetings talking about work rather than actually working.
review.Advice to management: My advice for management is that we need to keep the meetings at a minimum only for necessary daily planning.

review.Pros: The benefits of working at CDPHE are the great benefits. They offer a traditional pension plan, great health insurance, ample paid time off, and flexible/hybrid schedules.
review.Cons: The organization is very left leaning and in support of the governor, if you have differing political opinions here you will feel like an outsider.

review.Pros: The environment at Baird is substantially different than other private wealth management firms. It is one of the few places that actually puts the client's needs in front of your income. You also receive support from teammates, and it is not completely cutthroat.
review.Cons: The income is slightly below what the rest of the industry is paying. You are getting paid more into retirement accounts but less as compensation.

review.Pros: It's a good place to learn the industry. Very fast paced work environment, much learning on the go, different avenues to hone expertise. Good support structure and compensatory benefits.
review.Cons: Very long, unpredictable hours. On service demands often leave little room for downtime. No linear path for advancement and career progression may get easily stifled by existing seniority.
review.Advice to management: Invest more time on new hires to make them more inclined to stay as opposed to relying on cheap labor from high turnover.

review.Pros: The company is very positive in creating an atmosphere where you can learn a lot, you can experiment and you won't be criticized for failing.  Failing multiple times is acceptable if it eventually leads to success.  They also are positive about equality.
review.Cons: Lumen is putting a lot of their eggs in the AI basket.  More data centers is good for Lumen because the core business is moving data between data centers and not to the end users.  If the AI bubble bursts, they'll have got rid of the easy free money (voice services) and lost out.
review.Advice to management: Stand up for our real principles and ignore Trumps DEI nonsense.

review.Pros: Excellent benefits and compensation,  401k matching and retirement options, coworker camaraderie,  learning cross functional skills, plenty of overtime, opportunities , industry leader in private jets
review.Cons: Deadline workloads and hours are high, mandatory overtime. Promotions and raises feel political. Employees often complain about having a buddy system, favoritism which impacts career growth

review.Pros: I enjoy the people I work with a great deal. Other than that, I do not really like the place I work. It is tolerable, at best.
review.Cons: The schedule, pay, executive leadership, basically everything else one can come up with in their minds, this place is a major offender. Pretty sad in my opinion.
review.Advice to management: Pay your employees who are doing a great job better.

review.Pros: Flexible working environment, you can work remotely every day of the week, or in the office every day of the week, or some combination of both. Hours are almost entirely flexible as long as you make it to the twice weekly standups in person or on Zoom. Benefits are more than generous for a company of this type.
review.Cons: Not a lot of communication coming from management about current slowdown in client assignments. No one is entirely sure if the company is doing well or not, and management provides zero feedback on the state or the future of the company. Many feel the writing is on the wall and are actively searching for new situations.
review.Advice to management: If there are more client issues we need to know about, tell us. Most of us would love to stay here, but we're conflicted. We might even be able to help attract new clients. We're not exactly un-networked out here.

review.Pros: I think the people who are work with are a plus for me. The pay is pretty good for the area and since they are one of the two major hospital systems in the area the medical care is ok.
review.Cons: One of the two major hospital systems in the area and you know about american health care... other than that, lack of some specialties really holds us back i think.

review.Pros: The word "family" has become a red flag in recent years when discussing a place of business, and for good reason, but when it's something the employees feel as opposed to being something the employer assumes and demands, it can be a powerful testament to a business's strength. The Blackhorse has treated me, from day one, as a valued member of their team, investing in me professionally, financially, and personally. This is not unique to me. When you're an employee at the Pub, you are treated with the full scope of human dignity. No opinion is unheard, no situation is misunderstood. You are supported, so long as you support the goals of the business. It truly is the most encouraging and supportive work environment I've ever been involved with.
review.Cons: When working for a family-owned business, that has, over three decades, boot-strapped itself into becoming a local institution, there are of course areas that may frustrate new hires. The owners understand their business in and out, but sometimes that can lead to changes coming too slowly. It's also true that the income ceiling in an organization like this, no matter how successful they are, will never be fully commensurate with a more corporate, impersonal job.
review.Advice to management: As a member of management myself, all I can suggest is the same thing I tell the team every day: you are the stressed rope bridge between the ownership's vision and the employees' daily reality. It's your job to hold things together, and be a safe place for everyone's feelings to cross, no matter how heavy.

review.Pros: Great teamwork culture with very reliable support for job functions. Great time off policies and easy PTO requesting process. Very supportive management with monthly meetings for overall performance.
review.Cons: The pay is not that great compared to similar organizations. Also, there can be a very competitive atmosphere when applying to internal roles. Mentorship program is not the best as some mentors put in low effort with mentees.
review.Advice to management: Push for better pay, highlight job duties and distinguish between requirements vs expectations.

review.Pros: In a part-time setting, the work is straight forward. The work schedules are accomodating. You also have the opportunity to work in multiple departments and decide what works for you.
review.Cons: The cons are the long hours. TJX stores are open (for employees) from 7am to 10pm. Also the pay is not great nor are the benefits. Part-time works are not eligible for much.

review.Pros: The people genuinely want to do the right thing on behalf of the customers and patients. I like the people I work with on a regular basis.
review.Cons: Projects always seem to take a lot longer than they should to complete. There is a culture of non-commitment when direct answers are needed for planning / projections.

review.Pros: i have the freedom to run my warehouse how i see fit. I get to work with all kinds of people all year long. it is amazing
review.Cons: There is limited travel in this field if your not a driver. Even then its all work based so you dont get much away time.
review.Advice to management: There can always be more people that are helping make decisions for the gre3ater good. It does everyone benificits to get more imput on everything work related

review.Pros: Some of the benefits of working at ABC is free lunch mondays through thursdays, team building events, Summer Fridays, a hybrid work schedule, and convienent location in Midtown.
review.Cons: As a small non-profit, there is a heavy workload compared to the amount of staff. There is a high turnover rate, burnout, and interpersonal conflicts between coworkers.
review.Advice to management: n/a

review.Pros: The pros of working at NMH is that it is a well known company, and the pay working here is very competitive considering the market.
review.Cons: The cons of working at NMH is the lack of care from management, the lack of ongoing training, the lack of being able to move up in the company

review.Pros: Some of the pros working at UnitedOne Credit union is a great benefits program. The company also has reliable, friendly, and helpful peers to help you with onboarding and future tasks. The management team is responsible and clear.
review.Cons: Some of the work we do can sometimes pile up. It makes things stressful and work-load heavy at times. In addition, the departments are small so tasks are usually not delegated.

review.Pros: Working at StretchLab is such a great work environment! It mostly caters to individuals who have mobility or flexibility issues. The clients are great as well as the staff. I am going into the health and wellness field in the future, so working here is a great opportunity for me.
review.Cons: Sometimes the schedule does not fill. There are a lot of reasons why this could be happening. It also does get tiring as we are moving a lot throughout the shift.
review.Advice to management: none!

review.Pros: I work as a cook and the work is very fulfilling, I enjoy improving peoples' days with my cooking and the associates on the line with me are family so I'm glad to have this experience working with them. Also the club staff are friendly and often offer everyone shitfties, among other things throughout the day, which is very nice. Just happy to serve my community and be a part of an organization that acts as a family.
review.Cons: Sometimes working as a cook, or anything in a kitchen, can be stressful. Especially in a club bar, people can get routey and rush you when you're trying to work. Such things can and will happen in any kitchen environment.

review.Pros: The pros is the benefits, the friendships you make, the overall pay and working conditions. The cons, sometimes have to work a lot of hours
review.Cons: I thought I just answered that. It is the overall hours that you have to work just to make up for what you missed during the week
review.Advice to management: My advice would be to always treat every single employee equal and do your fair share of work

review.Pros: While TC Max is a small company, there are many opportunities to learn and advance, even learning outside of your "assigned" area. Ownership is happy to share their knowledge and help others learn
review.Cons: Flip side - it's a small company, so while you can learn a lot, there isn't much opportunity for further advancement to higher paying positions

review.Pros: It offers various opportunities to work cross functionally, gain experience in various industries or categories, and fairly good employee support (career growth, annual reviews, learning across org, etc)
review.Cons: The workload can be a lot, particularly when there are several competing deadlines. There is also too many meetings and some what layers of approval.  And the experience can vary depending on your team or manager. It is also a large company and you can get "overlooked" unless you advocate for yourself.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your employees and teams more, cut down on meetings, and simply be clear about priorities. Let people do their jobs without overcomplicating things..

review.Pros: I have a good work/life balance. I am in a good working situation where I feel safe at work and also supported by the supervisors. My pay is not too bad.
review.Cons: I'm never eligible for a raise and I feel like I may end up getting a pay cut at some point. I also have no room for growth and I'm teaching the same curriculum year after year.
review.Advice to management: I think they should let us move up into leadership positions. I'm a great employee so I'm stuck in my current role.

review.Pros: They have company provided insurance. My work schedule is very flexible. The people who work there are very nice and fun to be around. We do fun projects.
review.Cons: There is not a lot of upward mobility. Jobs rarely open up for people to apply for. The pay is not great. Feels like you are stuck.

review.Pros: It's a great company that provides growth opportunities as well as investments in education for growth. A brand loved by millions so it's exciting to help build that brand
review.Cons: There is high pressure to deliver sometimes to maintain the branding. Users have high expectations and it trickles down. Lots of shifting priorities constantly. This makes it difficult to maintain organizational order

review.Pros: Remote work, no cost health insurance, very liberal PTO and attendance policy, bonus incentives plus monthly incentives, paid holidays, working in a team environment, flexible hours
review.Cons: some agents are from overseas, there are metrics to adhere to, there are QA and LCA graded calls that are weekly, bonus is based off of metrics.
review.Advice to management: Treat everyone the same

review.Pros: The pay and benefit options are very good. We have a good work life balance for the most part and there are interesting travel benefits as well.
review.Cons: Everything occurs at the whim of politics so goals and objectives change regularly and significantly. Communication isn't great and promotion opportunities are limited without being willing to relocate.

review.Pros: Great work life balance. Lots of paid holidays and vacation. Local management is very supportive of you. They also have an incredible retirement matching program!
review.Cons: No stock incentives offered like other companies. They also have a hard performance culture. They force rank the top to bottom of employees. There is always a fear of layoffs.

review.Pros: Interesting work and dedicated coworkers, though the mission is somewhat obscured. Great projects happening in pockets, though not uniformly across the organization. Excellent work and life balance.
review.Cons: Organization can seem flattered with itself, and its sense of self-importance. Also walks a line between not-for-profit and for-profit. For-profit expectations, and not-for-profit salaries. Testing is interesting, rarely liberating.

review.Pros: Very flexible work environment, completely remote and great culture. The pay is also very competitive for the market. I love the coworkers I have as well
review.Cons: The work load can be a bit much during the year and there are times it feels isolating when everyone is fully remote. Culture can bit different across teams.

review.Pros: Freedom to make your own schedule and work as many or as little hours as you want. There is no minimum required. Daily office hours and trainings. Database of information to help with projects. Daily updates.
review.Cons: Abrupt ending to projects and waiting to get assigned to another. Faulty onboarding sometimes. Sometimes you can be mismatched to projects you aren't actually skilled to be on.

review.Pros: You can more or less make your own schedule and have alot of freedom on what you do. There are also alot of programs offered to you that you can use if you want.
review.Cons: Not alot of support. There may be programs, but there is still favoritism, and they don't seem to care about focusing on newer people. If you choose to leave, not a care is given.
review.Advice to management: If you support your team/workers more, they will feel and do better. I love working there but lost my passion and now hate it.

review.Pros: Employee recognition is good, we get a lot of job perks, we aren't micromanaged, the team is really supportive. I like the patients we serve as well.
review.Cons: Really nothing, other than being a remote employee makes it difficult to participate in bonding with coworkers outside of work, which is a small disappointment.

review.Pros: The distance of driving; retirement plan; hours of working; colleagues; benefits; ease of get off work; no weekend hours; no holidays; and work is not hard
review.Cons: I don't have the down time of driving from work to home; so sometimes I sit in the car when I get home before going in the house
review.Advice to management: appreciate your staff

review.Pros: Everyone at work is friendly  and we all get along. My boss understands certain things happen and is easy on her employees. Everyday is different and the customers are fun to interact with.
review.Cons: It can be busy and demanding at times and the work gets stressful. Certain nights things need to be done before we can go home and if it was a busy day, we need to stay after,.
review.Advice to management: None, they are understanding and friendly.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Oracle are the work life balance, an inclusive community that fosters relatonships, the ability to work remote and the on the job learning.
review.Cons: The cons of working at Oracle is the lack of opportunities to grow within the company. Opportunities for advancement seem to be reserved only for people who are aready in leadership.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Dell are that I am trusted in my role. I don't deal with micromanging. It is a high trust job.
review.Cons: The cons of working at Dell are that it is not the highest paying in my field. There is high turnover because of this reason.

review.Pros: They have a wide range of benefits. They have a wide array of projects and industries to work within. Most of the middle managers I have interacted with are supportive and do not micromanage. The higher level managers do frequent check ins across departments to gauge for investment and feedback.
review.Cons: Cross department support, communication, and training is a bit lacking which can slow down joint projects. When projects slow down it is always considered the fault of the current engineer and not anyone who handled the project before them. Organization of joint projects with outside companies are inconsistent and make it difficult when shifting from project to project.
review.Advice to management: Management should look to improving cross department communication and training so everyone understands what other departments jobs are and how to make sure the work transferring from one department to another is sufficient for each departments' quality requirements. This will prevent minor mistakes from piling up and slowing down projects.

review.Pros: The pros literally have nothing to do with ANY coworkers. Any benefits and good things all come from the experiences with patients and gaining wisdom on difficult work situations.
review.Cons: Horrible management and co workers that want to tear every ounce of confidence you have in order for you not to get ahead. They lie and manipulate and make you look bad when the allegations are absolutely are false even when you work is showing it
review.Advice to management: Find a new job, get new management.

review.Pros: Great organizational culture and leadership really cares about the employees. Amazing benefit package available to all employees and very generous retirement plans and contributions. Overall very great company.
review.Cons: The organization can by very hierarchical and there are many levels of management. Sometimes things can take a little longer to get done or approved due to all the levels of approval needed.

review.Pros: I feel that overall, Disney has a robust benefits package that I can't live without now. On site pharmacy, excellent medical and dental, and even a tuition program for college students. There's just so much here that makes it a wonderful place to spend your whole life.
review.Cons: I feel that suddenly we've been having way too many lay offs and so many good people have been let go just because of a bad economy. As well, the past few years had bad decisions from leadership that have hurt our products.
review.Advice to management: I feel that the lay offs need to end before more people move to other companies.

review.Pros: We get medical and dental insurance coverage, paid time off, employee discounts, 401k retirement plans, flexible setting (remote or hybrid) and there are company sponsored events.
review.Cons: The salary is not very competitive and the career growth is slow. Print media field is in decline so there maybe issue of job security.
review.Advice to management: none

review.Pros: I have worked here for over 4 years and have found that I feel like I am welcome on every unit that I may float to or visit.
review.Cons: Some areas and departments can have small cliques but it isn't bad over all. Everyone is nice but you should remain amicable only in those departments.
review.Advice to management: Reward staff more for hard work and support us when patients mistreat us

review.Pros: the people at the company are quite nice and they are fun to work with. there are ok benefits to the company. it is a good conversation starter working for the company
review.Cons: the pay isnt great, the company performance is terrible, leadership does not really care about the employees, somewhat immoral to work in the industry, cult like

review.Pros: The schedule flexibility makes it easy to maintain a healthy work/life balance, with plenty of time for personal or family needs. They also pay on time, and they offer rather substantial mental health benefits.
review.Cons: The pay is definitely the biggest drawback. Minimum wage for this type of emotionally intensive work is extremely disappointing. The lack of work available is the other biggest issue. Some days there's not a single task available no matter what time I log in.
review.Advice to management: Higher pay rates, hiring freeze, tasks prioritized toward long-term employees with strong rating histories.

review.Pros: Working for a global company gives a sense of security that I feel I would not have working for a small independent company. it also gives the ability to be able to move up in the company for people who want to be able to do that.
review.Cons: Working for such a large company I feel like a small fish in a big pond. I wonder if the higher ups even know I exist.
review.Advice to management: I have no advice.

review.Pros: High computing capacity, support many servers, application or users at once. Reliably, like centralized management and all, centralized facilities can provide controlled physical protection and security.
review.Cons: Long or irregular hours, repetitive task, high pressure and stress, risk of a very technical problem and all, required constant learning and many other things
review.Advice to management: Provide proper training and support.

review.Pros: The benefits are great.  Employees receive health care benefits, dental benefits, vision benefits, vacation time, sick time, flexible hours, etc.  Holidays and a short winter break off.
review.Cons: Very little career mobility exists at The University of Akron.  The pay is lower than other state higher education institutions in the region.  Some employees are kept around that should not have been kept around.
review.Advice to management: You paid a consulting firm to perform a pay and position evaluation a few years ago.  I do not believe that it was properly conducted nor implemented.

review.Pros: Staff and people that I work with. The schedule and hours are a pro. The pay could be better, but it's more than other places.
review.Cons: Staffing shortages which can be unsafe. Floating and sending staff to other units or departments due these staffing shortages. Not being able to work remotely.

review.Pros: There really are not any pros currently. But it has let me pay my bills for 12 years. The insurance is not great, the leadership worse.
review.Cons: Every single thing, and I wish I was exaggerating. They have made my last couple of years so miserable I can barely stand it. But again, they pay my bills

review.Pros: The pay and benefits are not terrible, however, the work-life balance is not sustainable. Policies at city-wide and school level are always changing and not in the best interest of the employees, resulting in low morale.
review.Cons: The inconsistencies and expectations from administration are not sustainable long-term. The lack of protection for teachers when it comes to student and families is upsetting. Additionally, teachers are expected to be highly educated but receive little respect and are not trusted to know best.
review.Advice to management: Put teachers as managers!

review.Pros: I love working with the elderly population. I enjoy being able to help people and their families. I also enjoy working with most of my co-workers.
review.Cons: Working in healthcare is not for the light hearted. Working 12 hour shifts is not easy on me or my body. We always have a staffing shortage which makes giving each patient proper attention difficult at times. Some of the upper management team are very unprofessional and make the enviornment toxic.
review.Advice to management: Listen to the staff about what works and what does not.

review.Pros: The pros to working at BCI are that the work is simple and the coworkers are fairly easy to get along with. They also have pretty decent work benefits.
review.Cons: The cons to working at BCI are that their is a lack of communication, There is also not too much room to move up and increase your pay.

review.Pros: Working at Progressive gives me the flexibility to work from home, which makes managing my day easier.  I appreciate the encouragement from my team and the opportunities to learn new skills and grow into different roles.
review.Cons: The call volume and back-to-back converstations can be draining especially when a complicated issue comes up.  Working from home is convenient, but getting timely help can be difficult when the training chat is busy or there is no dedicated person available.

review.Pros: i work remotely, they paid for me to get liscensed, during aep you can make a lot of money, and they provide equipment as well
review.Cons: low pay, changing schedules, bad leads, no  room for growth it seems, mentally draining, during lock in period you dont make much money, you can also be unexpectedly furloughed
review.Advice to management: to be more transparent, more pay, actually promote growth in the company

review.Pros: The best part of working at Oregon Vocational Rehabilitation is the ability to truly make a difference in peoples lives. Staff are educated, professional and in general try to do their best to help the people we serve. Work hours are reasonable and management allows a great deal of freedom to do the job the way the employees feel it needs to be done.
review.Cons: At times there can be a great deal of pressure when working with customers that have severe and persistent mental health challenges, houselessness, and at times drug and alcohol addictions,   Some staff have been hired with little to no counseling experience and expect the job to be more of a social service occupation where they act as case managers instead of rehabilitation counselors.
review.Advice to management: Management needs to do a better job of controlling the number of programatic changes and when they are required, do a better job of communicating out those changes to the employees.  Explaining the why behind the changes would go a long way to reducing frustration and anxiety.

review.Pros: The company is warm and welcoming.  They offer good benefits and promote the value of improving your career.  They keep the employees informed about the direction of the company and about the financial results on a regular basis.
review.Cons: The company is very left leaning and goes out of its way to promote progressive ideals.  They often lay off workers but at the same time spend money on town hall meetings with special speakers.

review.Pros: iT IS EASY TO CHOSE YOUR PROJECTS AND VERY EASY TO SCHEDULE YOUR HOURS THE WAY YOU WANT.  iF YOU NEED OFF YOU CAN SELECT THE HOURS THAT WORK FOR YOU.
review.Cons: tHERE ARE NO  BENEGITS.  nO HEALTH INSURANCE OR SICK TIME OR VACATION.  IF YOU TAKE OFF WORK YOU ARE GOING TO LOSE PAY ESPECIALLY IF YOU ALREADY SCHEULED TO WORK THAT DAY
review.Advice to management: TRY NOT TO ADD AND REMOVE MODS

review.Pros: Get to learn different techniques on different ways to cook or make something. They are willing to work with you when sick or family issues
review.Cons: Long hours, and it can get very hectic with having to do things fast pase. Also you may not have time to take a brake

review.Pros: teamwork, positive reinforcement, makes sure we have time for holidays and family. they are consistent with pay they provide training when needed as well and just great people to work for and work with
review.Cons: i honestly cant say there are any cons i have had no issues and i have been here for years. everyone is very friendly there is an open door policiy and i always mention how well everyone works together

review.Pros: Work from home and employer provided equipment. Management is extremely helpful with helping answer questions. Other employees are also very knowledgeable and helpful to new employees.
review.Cons: Timed calls. Very strict at following the manufacturers rules for warranties. Only a half hour lunch is hard to get used to after coming from a company where you had a lot more ease to take a minute to yourself.

review.Pros: The pros of working at LPL are the healthcare benefits, and there is room for advancement as well as different aspects of the job to explore, and has decent pay.
review.Cons: The negatives at working at LPL are that it is a bad work to life ratio, inflexible schedules, toxic upper management, underfunded organization which creates stressful staffing situations.
review.Advice to management: Required inter staff communication training

review.Pros: I love my assistant first of all...she's amazing.  I enjoy the class, and the majority of my coworkers.  It pays well and the benefits are solid as well.
review.Cons: Its in downtown atlanta, which can suck to get to, or from. I dont love admin, nor do I really understand/support some of the policies I have recently had the misfortune of learning about, as they relate to the kids.  There is a definite generational divide as well...older teachers/staff have one mindset, and younger/newer have their own .
review.Advice to management: Dont mircromanage, and dont automatically take the side of those that are older, just b/c you are of a similar age.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Hutchinson is it is a local company, it is very close to where I live.  Hutchinson is only a five minute drive from where I live.
review.Cons: The cons are mainly the management.  It is owned by a French company, the CEO and other higher ups don't live in America and the people they hired are not good at managing people.  They don't seem to take sexual harassment seriously as the building manager has been accused three times of sexual harassment in the past five years and they keep trying to sweep it under the rug.

review.Pros: The biggest pro is that I get to work from home. This saves on gas and commute times. Since gas prices are very high right now.
review.Cons: The company is terrible with micro managing. The supervisors that are supposed to be there to help you, don't answer half the time. The make you cross train and don't pay enough.
review.Advice to management: I have seen several reviews about the micro managing. It needs to be dealt with. Also the QA reviews need a bit more leniency

review.Pros: You get to do something that really gives back to the community, you make a difference in the lives of students, and in that sense it's much more fulfilling than some other jobs.
review.Cons: The pay is really not acceptable, especially when you consider how expensive it is to live in the city and the surrounding area. We also don't have enough staff to prevent the workload burning people out.
review.Advice to management: We need to hire more TA's and aides so that teachers can focus on instruction, classroom behavior management has become too much of a distraction

review.Pros: a supportive and inclusive working cultyure that welcomes the differences among people. above average benefits compared to other nonprofit organizations. generous PTO policy and healthcare coverage
