review.Cons: nonprofits in general do not pay as well as their for-profit countparts. resources to do the job may not be as up to date as one likes.

review.Pros: I'm working in the field of my choice for a great company that pays well and has room for advancement. I've moved up twice and gotten several raise over the course of 8 years.
review.Cons: Extreme temperatures, all the time. It's hot in the summer and cold on the winter plus I work on plants so I can't smoke at all.

review.Pros: Supportive colleagues, strong benefits packages, good retirement options.  The environment fosters support for continuing education and having resources to allow employees to further their education.
review.Cons: Large, bureaucratic system.  When there are problem employees, it can take a long time for anything to happen to them.  This brings down the morale of the team.

review.Pros: They provide fairly good benefits. Pension. 401k match. parental leave and sick time. family leave. average pto. Middle management cares. Some flexibility. fairly good job secuiryt
review.Cons: upper management does not care. some benefits have disappearted. return to office mandate. ceo calling employees lazy. lower pay than average. raises are on the lower side

review.Pros: Employee autonomy, relaxed atmosphere, friendly team, understanding ownership, typical hours with no overtime expectation, appropriate pay structure, close to home, administrative assistance provided, professional licensure covered by ownership
review.Cons: Poor patient base, very high cancellation rate amongst clientele, very low reimbursement rate for services provided, disorganized ownership, unclear expectations, shifting goal posts for success
review.Advice to management: Learn both the applicable practice side of the business as well as be more well-versed in the management of the business as well

review.Pros: The position is remote and for the most part the hours are extremely flexible. You are able to make your schedule assuming that tasks are available.
review.Cons: Lack of management engagement and communication. You are left to try and figure things out for yourself. There is no real "training" and no warnings about quality, you can be fired without warning.

review.Pros: I enjoy the fact that I can be autonomous in my role and provide solutions that generate positive financial returns for the clients that work with our investment fund.
review.Cons: I believe that we are under a lot of pressure to achieve high goals and demanding results for management as well as our clients as we need to achieve high financial returns in order to keep our clients satisfied.
review.Advice to management: I believe that it is best to be transparent as possible to our clients so that proper expectations and risks are clear and understood before the client decides to do business with us.

review.Pros: I have a lot of autonomy in how I do my job.  Most of my clients are appreciative and nice to deal with.  I don't have to get up early.
review.Cons: While the hourly pay sounds good, the total pay doesn't end up being great because most of my work isn't billable hours.  I work weeknights, so I miss out on music/social events.

review.Pros: The pros of being a employee of National Heritage academies are being able to work at your own pace. The organization also respects their employees.
review.Cons: The cons of being an employee of this organization are being able to perform at a high level. Each person is expected to well at any given moment.
review.Advice to management: Do your best.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Tampa Fire Rescue are good salary, variable workweek, second family, opened many opportunities outside of work, and it's a respectable job.
review.Cons: The cons of working at Tampa Fire Rescue are the politics involved, the egos you are surrounded with, the late nights, sleep deprivation, high cancer rates, and traumatic scenes.
review.Advice to management: Don't forget that you were once a rookie on the streets. Treat your subordinates how you would want to be treated.

review.Pros: Family owned company that treats it's employees like family. The only company that I've ever worked at that truly lives by its guiding principles, including "we are always learning" and "everything is a draft". One of the problems, though, is that with such a small company there's not a lot of opportunity for advancement.
review.Cons: Since there's less than 40 employees, there isn't a lot of room for advancement unless you're willing to hang around for years. There can also be a disconnect between upper management and the "worker bees". Not on purpose, but just because it just doesn't occur to management to share.
review.Advice to management: Remember that the lower-level workers also want to know what decisions are being made and why they're being made, even if they aren't involved in the process.

review.Pros: I am the owner and I make all decisions so I love my job. I have a steady full load so im always busy and I help people everyday
review.Cons:
If im shorthanded i have to hustle hard hard or my patient gets lil or no help and its not fair 
To them. So thats not good
review.Advice to management: No

review.Pros: I love being a part of a union. And i also love the people i work with. Not the managers so much but i love my co workers
review.Cons: Not being saying atta boy when you do a good job. You never get credit when you do a good job at something never ever

review.Pros: Location is great, the steady hours are predictable.  The benefits are competitive albeit in the sacrafice of raises/wages.  You have to take tests to qualify for the jobs you want to apply for, so it is competitive.
review.Cons: Cons can be hostile clients/general public.  Exposure to trauma if you work in law enforcement/child welfare/adult welfare.  Raises are few and far between, they get sapped by increases in the cost of living, inflation and rising health care premiums.
review.Advice to management: Do better at budgeting so that you can give the line workers raises rather than just yourselves and law enforcement.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Panda Express are the benefits. It's been awhile since I've had a job that offers health insurance, great pay, and PTO
review.Cons: The stressful working environment. I feel like i'm in prison all over again. We never get any wind down time. We are always expected to act accordingly.
review.Advice to management: Stop being so strict.

review.Pros: The greatest pro is that I get to work from home with a flexible schedule.  The pay rate is pretty good for what I do.
review.Cons: They tend to micromanage.  They treat us like we are five years old.  They demand overtime every week.  They change rules all the time with no explanation why and no apparent reason either.
review.Advice to management: My advice would be to hold individuals accountable for doing what they are supposed to do.  Management does not do that.  If they see a process isn't working, rather than drill down and see if the root cause is a poor worker or two, they will change the entire process which usually makes the workload easier for the poor worker and tougher for the good worker.

review.Pros: I get to do what I want. I work night shift and I do what is asked of me and I get some free time in the night
review.Cons: the people that come in at night can be drunk or not that nice. People sometimes sit in the parking lot for hours at a time and sometimes I want to go outside to enjoy fresh air.
review.Advice to management: Nothing

review.Pros: Good company, good benefits, innovative. They are a leader in their industry for contract service organization for pharma companies. They have a good reputation. They treat their employees fairly.
review.Cons: They're very competitive so they're always trying to cut costs and be the leader. This could mean cutting jobs and roles that aren't very essential.

review.Pros: It feels more like a family than an organization. Everyone is very friendly and kind and will go out of the way to help with anything that they can.
review.Cons: The main con is how far of a distance I have to drive to get to work. I also don't always like the hours that I have to work.

review.Pros: It's very interesting work, there is always something to do.  The pay is also pretty good for the job.  There are a lot of different sites you can work at
review.Cons: The benefits are not very good.  40 hours of PTO and it never increases, even after years of service.  Promotions are very limited and communication with leadership is spotty at best
review.Advice to management: delegate more and when asked a question, don't make something up if you don't know the answer

review.Pros: Pros for working for Twenix is that you get to choose the hours you want to work. The only con is that work can be slow and not guaranteed on a daily basis.
review.Cons: The only con is that there are slow times during the year and you aren't guaranteed work during the hours of availability. This is more common during summer months.

review.Pros: I have been able to keep a job for 10 years even after moving to several different states. I also made it through several layoffs and the COVID-19 pandemic. So, it's a stable job.
review.Cons: It is an unpredictible job and they make us do too much with too few resources. The pay also isn't that great. I don't wake up excited to go to work on any day.
review.Advice to management: Stop trying to do too much.

review.Pros: The pros of working at my company is the pay, the benefits, and the owners are wonderful. We get bonuses twice a year and they care about the employees.
review.Cons: right now, the cons are, we cant work remotely, and we aren't provided with a gas stipend so it's really expensive to drive to work.

review.Pros: The benefits are pretty decent. Not outstanding, but decent. Sick leave, vacant, holidays, plus an acceptable healthcare plan.  In my role we were flexible as far as working conditions and could work remotely with supervisory approval.
review.Cons: Salaries are lower than comparable private sector jobs, and raises weren't guaranteed.  In my org unit there was a lot of favoritism, and some of the management staff weren't skilled in management at all.
review.Advice to management: Stop playing favorites - treat everyone fairly. Also, if you work 12+ hour days, don't complain to other staff about it - you can offload some of that work or just leave on time like eveyrone else does. And lastly, enough with the endless Teams meetings.  Way too many people chat non stop and extend them for way too long.

review.Pros: Bright Horizons is deeply invested in employee wellbeing and growth.  Management, including C-suite, is accessible and responsive to employee feedback and concerns as well as employee innovation.
review.Cons: The medical benefits are horrible.  There are two main business sectors and one of the sectors struggles to keep up with innovation and the speed of business and technology today which has an impact on the other sector.
review.Advice to management: Improve the medical benefits.

review.Pros: They have good pay for the area, and although it has gotten worse over the years, their benefits package is still very good. There are many opportunities to further your education and advancement throughout the organization, since we mostly hire internally for management positions and above.
review.Cons: Yearly raises tend to be on the low side. It's a very big and bureaucratic organization, so change and big decisions tend to be slow. They charge employees for parking.
review.Advice to management: I think there are currently too many non-clinicians, with multiple associate managers and other positions that just add costs without delivering patient value, the primary mission. Same for having a large marketing budget while our hospital are chronically full so we don't need more patients (and shouldn't advertise widely like we're McDonalds anyway).

review.Pros: dealing with patients could really be frustrating sometimes, we get to attend to lots of patiemts and it could really be stressful and we leavework late
review.Cons: our pay is really nice and there are lots of benefits attached to working there, we are also eligible for health care benefits and they ten to treat us well

review.Pros: The mission is worthwhile and the organization is very effective. They are saving lives every day. I enjoy the people I work with and the CEO is fantastic.
review.Cons: The culture is toxic. There is no trust. Gossip is rewarded. My job is routine and mundane. I am not given the opportunity to grow.
review.Advice to management: Trust the people you hire to do their jobs. Stop rewarding people who tattle on their teammates.

review.Pros: There is continuous opportunity for career growth and learning, and constant exposure to diverse clinical cases and advanced healthcare frameworks. There is also opportunity to build valuable and cross functional relationships.
review.Cons: There is high patient case loads which leads to emotional and mental strain. Also, there is rapid population growth, which means that our departments are stretched thin on most days.

review.Pros: I am able to have good work hours so that I can spend more time with my family. I am able to have summers off so that I can spend time with my son.
review.Cons: One con is the pay. Education is such an underpaid profession. Another con is the amount of things that you have to deal with and is acceptable at schools.

review.Pros: The working environment is safe and all employees are very valued, the working culture has instilled team work. It also allows us to express ourselves with our abilities.
review.Cons: I work in a position that requires direct interaction with customers daily and human beings can be the most trying organisms. One minute something happens and you just want to scream.

review.Pros: You can make your own schedule and you can ask for new accounts if your existing accounts running out of work. Your supervisors generally leave you alone.
review.Cons: Very little compensation for the job you're doing. They expect errorless work for just about minimum wage. Some of the clients are very difficult to understand.

review.Pros: I mostly have control over the work I do and feel like I have freedom to complete tasks on my terms. The pay is decent, and the work is fulfilling.
review.Cons: It can be very stressful during peak seasons, and I frequently have to work long shifts without time off, including back to back 13 hour days.
review.Advice to management: Try to give employees more of a choice in how long they work and whether or not they want to pull back to back long shifts.

review.Pros: I love working here because of potential career growth. The projects are exciting and challenging, my colleagues are always ready to help out and the overall office vibe keeps us motivated
review.Cons: The meetings usually take up too much of the workday, reducing productivity. We hold late night virtual meetings and end up feeling exhausted on the following morning.

review.Pros: working at a hotel has many pros such as meeting people from different countries , learning customer service and communication skills , getting the  opportunity for  growth and promotion , having job stability , receiving tips and benefits and gaining experience in hospitality industry which is useful world wide
review.Cons: The cons of working at a hotel includes long and irregular working hours , working on weekends and holidays , dealing with difficult or rude customers
review.Advice to management: management should focus more on staff welfare , fair shift scheduling , regular training

review.Pros: It is a great opportunity to make a real difference and its good if you enjoy being on your feet and exploring the different neighborhoods of the city.
review.Cons: Terrible work culture and poor leadership. Turnover is rampant and institutional knowledge is unfairly loaded onto a few people. Physically exhausting during the busiest times of the year.

review.Pros: My job is completely remote and I can work from anywhere in the world. My work hours are completely flexible. I can work any time 24/7 and take off work any time I want to.
review.Cons: The cons of my job is that work availability is not guaranteed. Pay is not guaranteed. There are no benefits at all such as health, dental, vacation pay, sick pay.

review.Pros: one of the biggest pros of working at omnicom is the opportunity to work within a global network of leading agencies with world-class clients.it offers excellent learning, career growth and exposure to innovative marketing
review.Cons: like many large global agency groups, working at omnicom can be fast paced and high pressure with tight client deadlines. the structure can sometimes feel bureaucratic, and workloads can be heavy
review.Advice to management: continue to invest in employee wellbeing, work-life balance and  clearer internal communication

review.Pros: A strong sense of mission among staff, with ample resources dedicated to professional development to help staff succeed in their many diverse responsibilities, while also maintaining a strong connection to the community.
review.Cons: Recent structural changes in the organization have diverted resources from the institution's primary mission, with an expanding bureaucracy that limits the impact of traditional activities.
review.Advice to management: Invest in the people, programs, and policies that are most closely aligned with the organization's mission.

review.Pros: The pay is within market ranges and merit raises are at time very generous. Employee engagement is okay and they treat older workers well and nicely.
review.Cons: Employee engagement surveys are just something on a checklist. Work groups are formed to address low scoring sections but then the suggestions are simply filed in the trash.

review.Pros: Upon hire you receive if elected medical, dental, vision, etc. You can also have a 401k with match through the company and elect to purchase stocks through the company. PTO is also given and Macy's Inc also gives their employees a discount for purchases for the stores or online.
review.Cons: For my role, there isn't much to say in terms of Cons of working at Macy's Inc. I can see from the in-store employees that they have more pressure in getting sales.
review.Advice to management: N/A

review.Pros: The job is one hundred percent remote and for them most part I set my on hours. As long as I accomplish the work that I'm given within the deadlines I'm given, I am mostly left to set my own schedule and do as I please.
review.Cons: Working in the consulting industry, especially for such a small company, the pay is not as competitive and there is the real worry of being laid off if the work dries up. The uncertainty that comes with that can be concerning and would be one of the main factors I consider if I decide to seek other employment.
review.Advice to management: More transparency from management would be nice. The process involved in determining salaries and bonuses is completely hidden, and employees are discouraged from discussing our pay with one another. It would go a long way if management was open about how they think the company is doing and what the outlook is for work for the next year to two years.

review.Pros: I work in the corporate offices of Meijer and feel that it is a great place to work.  We have tons of benefits provided to us with Meijer constantly doing things to prove how much they care about their employees. You can see all the time how much of a family environment it is with work life balance valued.
review.Cons: In the finance area there is a limited spaces for growth.  It’s very linear with little in between roles or promotion room available to us.

review.Pros: Challenging work, decent pay and benefits.    Team based environment and some travel opportunities.   Plus they have a sushi bar in the building for lunch.   Lots of opportunities to advance career or make lateral moves.
review.Cons: 4 days a week in the office.  Constant restructurings and layoffs.   lots of red tape to get things done and very centralized beaucracy upper management.    Things move very slow
review.Advice to management: none

review.Pros: Pros for working at Meijer is you always have coworkers you can talk to if you need help most of the time you don’t even have to ask because as a team we all work together to help each other get done with our projects. You can easily advance to a higher status within my corporation. What I also love is Meijer corporation stands with DI and there is zero tolerance for any type of bullying racism any type of prejudice. Meijer corporation makes you. Feel safe when you walk in the door because you know it’s a zone free of judgment.
review.Cons: I I have worked for Meijer corporation and I really can’t tell you. There’s many times because it really isn’t at all not for me and everyone I know never really complains either we get paid fairly decent. You can move up quickly like I can’t sit and lie and say that there’s cons to my job when I don’t feel that there is any type of cons
review.Advice to management: My advice to management is always check on your subordinate’s make sure they’re not experiencing burnout in the workplace any type of bullying. Make sure they feel comfortable and they understand their job. Well, always keep in touch. Communication is key and ultimately teamwork is a dream work and any manager knows that.

review.Pros: The staff is really big on teamwork. There are always people willing to help you learn and improve. You get a 50% discount on all food items.
review.Cons: The company favors customers over employees in every conflict. If there is a regular customer that intentionally makes you uncomfortable or commits stolen valor for a discount (and admits to doing so), nothing will be done about it. Most of the restaurant and district managers know each other. This means that it is difficult to report management or transfer to another store if you aren't getting along with your manager. The customers are set in their ways. There is never any guarantee that you'll make more than $10/hour and, where I live, that's less than 2/3 of minimum wage.

review.Pros: HHSC is a state-run organization, with union representation, so there are great benefits when compared to private organizations. These benefits include more job security, built-in pay raises, good health insurance and generous sick and vacation days.
review.Cons: The cons are a lot of paperwork, red tape and oversight due to being a state organization, slow to adopt newer technologies and make changes.
review.Advice to management: Things could be better if management actively pursued improving weak spots by taking in input from staff and advocating for positive changes.

review.Pros: safe, nice environment to work with super nice people, colleagues, supervisors, etc. diverse workforce with lots of opportunities to learn about cultures and progress as a human being.
review.Cons: the work stress can sometimes get to you and lead to burnout, super fast paces environment to work at and very emotionally and physically demanding.

review.Pros: The culture and vision of the company is something I am proud to work for. The sustainability aspect of what we are trying to for the world is important.
review.Cons: The culture and the start-up nature of the business is difficult. Everyday is different and there are not standard processes in place which makes it very ambiguous to be involved in.
review.Advice to management: NA

review.Pros: Good pay , good benefits , local operation so i dont have to travel far , stable work environment . Managment seems to be competant and isnt too bad.
review.Cons: Co workers can be difficult to work with , many differnt backgrounds are working at the same time and this can lead to issues , PTO could be better , benefits could be more affordable
review.Advice to management: increase moral amongst your employees and good things will follow.

review.Pros: I love the flexibility of work and the companionship with my colleagues. I greatly enjoy mentoring students. I am free to work hard and make meaningful change.
review.Cons: The pay structure is fixed, and so raises only come from promotion. There are also some challenges related to students overstepping faculty and bringing demands to the provost.

review.Pros: Some pros of working at Navy Federal Credit Union is they have a great bonus structure. They really try to encourage their employees with the bonus.
review.Cons: The cons of working for Navy Federal Credit Union is that it seems like leadership has no real skills in people management which can be frustrating. They promote individual contributors into people management roles.

review.Pros: The pros of working at a IUB include access to premium healthcare as well as moderately high compensation with access to the arts, sciences, and technology.
review.Cons: The cons of working at IUB include long hours, inequities in the workplace that impact compensation as well as competitiveness and staff morale. Advancement is also difficult for some who work at IUB.

review.Pros: Pros are my coworkers and clients. Con is the pay is minimal for all the work that is expected of all of the firms employees.
review.Cons: The cons are that the salary/compensation are not what I had expected considering Wilmington Health is a larger corporation and I thought they would be able to pay more than they do.

review.Pros: The are many pros of working at Meetings and Incentives Worldwide. The executive team treats all of the employees like family and they truly care about everyone. The flexible nature of the work environment is especially commendable. They really allow employees to be there for their families when needed. They also highlight and honor work that is done well and highlight some fabulous employees regularly.
review.Cons: While there aren't many cons of working for Meetings and Incentives Worldwide, the one thing that comes to mind is the required annual in person meeting. It started out great when they first had it but it has become stale and they really need to change it up a bit. The atmosphere is welcoming but the topics seem repetitive year after year.
review.Advice to management: Look at changing up the annual employee meeting. This could mean changing to a new location, a different time of year, new/fresh activities. Focus on individual team meetings more.

review.Pros: Flexibility, ability to work from home, average pay for the state I live in, solid communication from some members o management and supervisors, and that's it
review.Cons: The cons are being everley micromanaged in every aspect of the job, sometimes management has severe case of favoritism, the supervisors expect you to work nonstop

review.Pros: BYU is a very supportive environment. They value families. BYU also invests heavily into new faculty with a high tenure rate (i.e., >90%). I feel supported and set up for success.
review.Cons: As with any large institution, it can be difficult to get traction for certain tasks. There can be some administrative holdups, but generally these cons are minimal and greatly outweighed by the pros.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Olive Garden are that there's room to move up the chain compared to other food & beverage establishments. I get breakfast, lunch, and dinner on the house.
review.Cons: There is an unusually high turnover rate at my establishment in my city, and I don't get much time off, nor can I afford to, especially these days.
review.Advice to management: I would keep the hours flexible. That's my only real concern. There's no room to negotiate my hours because of the high turnover rate, which leaves me picking up the slack. I believe better communication would be a plus as well, although he's pretty laid-back for being a manager in a restaurant.

review.Pros: Gonzaga University is a highly respected employer in my city; many people work their entire career at this university. The benefits are outstanding and the leadership team encourages work life balance.
review.Cons: The staff pay is somewhat low compared to similar jobs in the private sector, and there is always the threat of layoffs because of budget concerns.
review.Advice to management: I would encourage management to offer incentives for stellar employees.

review.Pros: I enjoy my job and my team of five other teachers.  We have good health insurance.  My immediate supervisor is easy to talk to and is supportive.
review.Cons: It is one of the lower paying districts in my area.  It is very political with admin hiring people they know and not always who is best for the job.

review.Pros: It is a company that you can work at and be fine for many years to come. One of the best places to work at.
review.Cons: There are hardly any cons at IBM. Compared to everyone else IBM made sure to be a true and honest company. The rest do not.

review.Pros: Pros of working at costco is that you have pretty good and affordable benefits, time and a half on sundays, decent amounts of vacation and sick pay. Costco is pretty generous with approving time off requests
review.Cons: The cons of working at costco is that it is very physically challenging and demanding on your body. The members who shop at costco can be very entitles. Costco is very fast paced
review.Advice to management: Please regain the old costco mindset of taking care of the employees

review.Pros: Pros of working for Ahold Delhaize are strong financial benefits, comprehensive wellness support, flexible schedules, opportunities for growth and career progression, great community and culture.
review.Cons: Some of the cons of working at Ahold Delhaize are low starting wage and raises, demanding physical environment, sometimes difficult schedules and or flexibility strains.
review.Advice to management: Managers need to provide clear communication to store employees about labor and scheduling.  They also need to show strong support for frontline associates.

review.Pros: Flexible schedule, hands-off management style, can take as many breaks as needed as long as the work is done, solid amount of contract work at full time hours
review.Cons: Low pay, lack of management support, dismal working environment, lack of cohesion among co-workers, work is repetitive and dull, management tends to chase trends and does not know what made them successful in the first place
review.Advice to management: AI is a trend and not the panacea that make better workers. Supporting your employees makes better workers, not the computer.

review.Pros: Piano teaching can be a very solitary activity, and working at the school gives me access to a variety of colleagues and people in the larger piano pedagogy community.
review.Cons: Even though I have been at the school for 14 years, there is still a hierarchy, and decisions are not transparent.  The school also takes a lot of the student payment, and I can make more going only private.
review.Advice to management: Not sure if this will be shared, so I will not share.

review.Pros: Physical labor and alot of walking would be the cons of working for this company. Especially coming from previous work from home positions. Its definitely a challenge.
review.Cons: I apologize, I accidently answered the pros question with my cons answers. Ill put pros here: the pros of working for the company is getting weekly pay on Wednesdays. I have a good group of people I get to work with that I like.

review.Pros: At Citron Hygiene, I can leave my work at home, enhance my own knowledge and abilities, and work in an environment where I make a difference!
review.Cons: I feel like at times the work can become boring and sometimes overwhelming. I also feel like it can be very hard to move up in the company

review.Pros: I'm a senior service probider with a large clientele, and my boss is appreciative and treats me well.  She sometimes gives me little perks I didn't expect as a thank you.
review.Cons: Being a small business, there are no benefits.  Healthcare, retirement, any other perk like that are not offered.  I'm completely on my own for those things.
review.Advice to management: Setting up a 401K, and offering access to afordable healthcare, even if not contributing to it.

review.Pros: We receive ample breaks during the year, which means we get a week off every month. There is also never a dull moment during the work day.
review.Cons: The classrooms are over crowded. The students are not on grade level. There is the over hanging threat of an active shooter incident happening (or some other safety concern).

review.Pros: You get the privilege of shaping young minds, and you get to meet great people along the way which is nice. It is a very rewarding experience.
review.Cons: Sometimes you have to deal with unruly people or children. Sometimes parent's blame you for their child's short comings and behavior issues. It can be hurtful and discouraging when that happens.
review.Advice to management: Please listen to your employees' concerns, and do not just ignore them expecting it to go away.

review.Pros: Great culture, good benefits, ability to move up in departments is encouraged. Prioritizes internal development. Takes care of their workers. Encourages team work and team growth.
review.Cons: Some internal factors where it can be stressful to be a public entity, such as budget season. Some internal politicking can be an influence in a negative way.

review.Pros: Everyone is super deep and caring because they are all Christians. The org has a really healthy work/life balance and systems in place to promote that.
review.Cons: Sometimes it feels like they hire too many young people without real-world experience who just want a ministry job. I don't feel super challenged all the time by smarter people.
review.Advice to management: Hire people out of the business world who want to be part of a faith org.

review.Pros: is the best place I have ever worked, the pay is good for me and the environmet is also cool for me. Colleagues are also super nice
review.Cons: There are not so many cons here apart from the fact that we can meet varuiu chakkenges when doing deliveries like dogs and a rude customer
review.Advice to management: Continue same mngt style

review.Pros: The pros of working for Oconee Comfort is that the workplace truly feels like a home. The managers care as well as the employees. We also deliever a top notch product and job, so it makes it a place to say that I am proud to work for.
review.Cons: I think that the pay could be a little better considering the amount and type of work that we do. But overall, the environment and flexible schedule make it all worth it.

review.Pros: I am off on nights and weekends with the exception of one half Saturday a month. My boss is understanding when I need to take time off.
review.Cons: Sometimes things change and it is hard to adapt. I wish I could retire but if I have to have a job right now I'm glad it's this one.

review.Pros: I have a lot of autonomy in my daily workflows, it's a fully remote position, and I've been able to grow my skillset and build a new professional network.
review.Cons: The SEO industry is struggling, Google is making data collection difficult, we don't move fast enough to implement new features to stay ahead of the competition.

review.Pros: You get your own office and have a lot of autonomy to do your job the way you see fit.  They also have a very aggressive compensation plan
review.Cons: If you miss any days due to illness or vacation, there is no one there to pick up your slack.  You have to get your files from a to z
review.Advice to management: NO

review.Pros: There are lots of opportunities to work overtime, and the company offers good benefits. I also like that it offers leave if an employee becomes sick, pregnant, etc. I also like my coworkers.
review.Cons: The base pay is not great. I have to work overtime to make a decent salary. Some of the people in upper management also suck.

review.Pros: The pros are that I am able to make decisions by myself about what I teach.  I also like my co workers, and the environment is relaxed.
review.Cons: The cons are bad communication, weak leadership, students running the school in terms of getting to do what they want, and not following through on plans.
review.Advice to management: na

review.Pros: They have a lot of job positions and opportunities available that can suit how you want to contribute overall. So all in al there is alot you can do
review.Cons: The jobs are very monotonous and repetitive. Sometimes it feels like it sucks the life out of you, given how the whole system operates. Really pulseless

review.Pros: The work environment provides engaging challenges every day.  Management will take notice of those who want to learn management skills and grow to higher levels within the organization.  Fantastic first job and lots of opportunity for growth.
review.Cons: Schedule is flexible but demanding.  Requires working nights, weekends, and holidays.  Burn out can occur in repetitive job roles.  Customer facing positions can require advanced problem solving skills and the ability to read emotions.
review.Advice to management: Always remember what your first day in the industry was like.

review.Pros: The pros of working at this organisation is the pay is higher than other organisations with similar roles and the culture is very tight knit
review.Cons: The work load is far too excessive and the practicing veterinarian doctors tend to disregard lower employees time, often working overtime or past closing without care

review.Pros: The boss is a very nice guy. He's understanding,  thoughtful, and helps out when we fall behind and need an extra hand. He helps the workers any way that he can
review.Cons: The only cons that i can think of are that there is only so many workers and if one person misses a day it gets harder for everyone

review.Pros: I get good benefits, and good salaries. I can work hybrid, which is easy to keep balance between work and family. The leader is considerate
review.Cons: There might be time I have to work on weekends. There are periods with high stress, especially when it is in the middle of the year and at the end of the year

review.Pros: I am able to create a fun and positive environment for our clients while steadily learning to build a path towards my future career choices and outcomes.
review.Cons: Here recently the pay has not been feasible to live a comfortable life. During this time our economy is not doing so well, and add in the most recent wave of inflation it's not making it easy to live life.
review.Advice to management: Invest less in current/future aspirations and grant the operations team that extra funding,

review.Pros: The pros are that I am able to work with students and families in a really meaningful way with skilled and helpful colleagues both inside and outside of my own department.
review.Cons: The cons are the challenges that come with funding in a public school system, like in any public school system. There are also teacher vacancies that significantly impact our ability to do our job well.

review.Pros: The pros of working at WOLFF is the freedom. I can basically do anything I want, as long as work is getting done in a timely manner.
review.Cons: The cons are the repetitiveness of the work. I virtually do the same thing every single day and it gets draining. Also, the 12 hour shift days could be exhausting

review.Pros: My job is fully remote and it appears it will stay that way. The home office is only 20 min from me so if there is an issue I can go there.
review.Cons: The pay at this job is very low. Leadership is not open to any improvements or suggestions. The company has not been operating properly therefore there are constant layoffs.
review.Advice to management: Listen to the people who are ACTUALLY doing the work. Just because you have been doing stuff a certain way for decades does not mean it is the right or only way.

review.Pros: There is a strong sense of community and support among the teams. I never feel like I am left behind or do not have anyone to go to for help.
review.Cons: It does take a while to be hired on full time, as they start most new hires as temp employees through third parties instead of doing their own recruiting.
review.Advice to management: None, so far have nothing but positive experiences with how they manage their teams.

review.Pros: I would say pros include being able to hone your programming and technical skills through the work, and also being able to stick to typical 9-5 working hours instead of longer hours.
review.Cons: The cons of working at IBM include a lack of impactful projects, relatively frequent layoffs and downsizing, and an overall sense of being behind many other tech companies when it comes to the latest developments.

review.Pros: My coworkers are supportive and kind. They are also collaborative and look out for the bests interests of their students. We also have freedom in designing our lessons.
review.Cons: The pay is low for our area. The job can also be very stressful in terms of classroom management and the responsibilties that we have in addition to teaching.

review.Pros: They value their employees, solid work/life balance, fun atmosphere. They really treat their employees well, and we get good benefits. They offer us free tickets to concerts sometimes, too.
review.Cons: Sometimes the hours can be a lot, especially on event days. There are also some departments that don't work as much as others, yet they get more pay.

review.Pros: It is a fairly hands-off working environment in my case. But my recruiter and the actual client largely influence this more than the company itself.
review.Cons: It exists to provide contract work to external clients. Because it is contract work, they can get away with not providing paid holidays or vacations, etc.
review.Advice to management: Just because they can legally avoid providing benefits to workers shouldn't mean they actually don't.

review.Pros: I work remote which is awesome.  I also have a busy schedule but can earn bonuses.  I have a great relationahip with my coworkers and enjoy working with the schools that I do
review.Cons: Sometimes organization is messy.  We recently added new software which has created a lot of headaches.  We are trying to work through tough management and some incompentence

review.Pros: There really are no pros of working at this organization. If I had to list one it would be networking with like minded new hires and collaborating on ideas of what else we could do with our insurance producers license to actually earn an income.
review.Cons: There are many cons of working here. First is the dishonest recruitment script they use to hire people. Then is the dishonest sales script that they reprimand us for straying from. Also, they tell you at the time of interview that you'll be able to make your own hours but then treat you poorly if you don't log on for 10-12 hours a day. They tell you that you're not coachable even if you follow their methods and instructions exactly then complain about many weeks of no income. They promise you a "doctors salary" but once you figure out it is impossible to earn that working for them they tell you that it takes many years to become profitable as if you were supposed to know that when you were leaving a real job to go there. I have been told by my supervisor to skip paying my car payment because a small mark on my credit score is worth the money I'll make later if I lock in now. He also told me to cry to my landlord and beg them to find me a roommate as if that would ever be there responsibility. I have been told to give up my home and ask my mother if I can sleep on her couch even though that would never be an option for me. Not to mention the "great free leads" they promise are just a list of 100 people per month that scream and yell at you because they have been asking to be put on the do not call list for years at this point.
review.Advice to management: do better. stop lying. be better.

review.Pros: Good work/life balance, friendly, energetic  atmosphere, no weekends/nights/holidays. The work is often physically demanding but satisfying, and management is very supportive for the most part.
review.Cons: The pay is pretty terrible, even on a management level. New employees start out at minimum wage, no exceptions.  The job itself is often in cold environments (coolers, freezers) that might not be for everyone.
review.Advice to management: Need to consider the team better and push back on corporate demands.  Employees are getting stretched to their limit.

review.Pros: The benefits are good: 15 days of vacation time and 10 days of sick time are separate. We get 10 holidays off and they have a matching 401K
review.Cons: They require us to be in the office 3 days a week, but it's not the same three days for everyone, so we're still sitting on Teams all day instead of collaborating in person. The marketing department head has a short temper and no one can disagree with him
review.Advice to management: Management needs to get into the office once in a while and realize that RTO has been a waste of time and resources

review.Pros: There is a lot of diversity so you get to wok with a variety of people  walks of life. There is opportunities to develop professionally if you chose to take on these opportunities.
review.Cons: Being able to advance your career can be limited and the time invested (years to get there) can seem daunting especially for older more skilled workers with years of service.   There is often favortism as well for these opportunities.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your employees without judgement or repercussions.

review.Pros: We are a small mechanical engineering firm that specializes in the restoration of historic buildings. It is very satisfying to stand back and look at our work, as I feel that it is important to salvage / upscale buildings that would have otherwise been destroyed. It is a very rewarding job, on many levels.
review.Cons: Sometimes it can get a bit repetitive, and as a small firm (6 people) we can easily get overwhelmed by the amount of work. We occupy a VERY specific niche, so I don't like turning away work. So, unfortunately, I get nervous about turning away work.
review.Advice to management: Always make sure that you appreciate your employees. I make sure that I provide bonuses, and other incentives to keep my staff loyal and happy.

review.Pros: The opportunities I get to make a difference to people it matters. Getting to teach Black students and work with udnerserved patients if very important for me
review.Cons: Uppermanagement and pay. I could get paid much more doing the same thing, many other places. Also management in my company is not very great.
review.Advice to management: They need to be more open to listening to people who work here

review.Pros: Age 55 and/or 15 years of service retirement opportunity. Great work life balance.  Good pay.  Work from home options. Also there is room for advancement here.  Great place to grow career wise and educationally.
review.Cons: The only real cons of working here is that diversity can be scarce depending on the department you are wanting to go into.  Posting or applying internally can be more about who you know rather than if your actually qualified for the role.
review.Advice to management: N/A

review.Pros: Everyone is helpful and wants to do the best job we can for the average American. It provides a livable wage and allows me to challenge and grow myself.
review.Cons: We are facing a lot of legislative challenges due to being a quasi government agency. We are stuck in a political battle between Republicans and Democrats and everyone loses.
review.Advice to management: Need to figure out the legislative issues.

review.Pros: I work mostly remote, which is really nice because I have improved work-life balance. I also get to work in a team that allows me to do a lot of new tasks that I can leverage heavily for future positions.
review.Cons: The company turnover is somewhat high, which concerns me because I am relatively new at the company and to the workforce in general. I want to stay at this company for at least a year or two, and I'm anxious to see how much turnover will take place/whether I will be a part of it.
review.Advice to management: N/A

review.Pros: All associates get a 20% store discount with occasional double discount periods, there is flexible scheduling available for part time employees, and the ability to cross train if you want to pick up more hours.
review.Cons: Managers frequently change schedules with little to no advance notice, the pay is awful and not at all worth the workload, almost always understaffed due to payroll restraints, stressful performance metrics that impact hours.

review.Pros: work life balance, PTO,, supportive leadership and very communicative amongst peers of the company, working together across different departments is highly encouraged by team leaders.
review.Cons: salary pay hours employee turnover and new faces not knowing whether someone you enjoyed working with would still be employed at the company which is worrisome

review.Pros: good PTO, benefits, a lot of different departments to work with, feel like I'm making a difference, non-profit so can get loan forgiveness (if that stays around)
review.Cons: lack of communication between departments, leadership can be wishy washy, grant funded so it can be nerve wracking to know if there funding will be there for jobs

review.Pros: The pros of working at Walmart in the department that I work in is that I get to choose what days and hours of the week thatI want to work and I work pretty independently.
review.Cons: The cons of working at Walmart is that the upper management treats people that are below them like they are just nothing compared to them.
review.Advice to management: My advice for management would be to get down eye to eye with your employees and spend a couple days in their shoes. It takes giving respect to get respect in return.

review.Pros: It's a ministry that shared the gospel of Jesus Christ with the poor and homeless, and there's great opportunities to share and live the good news.
review.Cons: In more recent years we've had quite a bit of changes in the leadership and that has made things difficult as an organization, and much more instability than in the past.
review.Advice to management: Be stable, remember it's a ministry, and make sure the gospel is the first priority.

review.Pros: The pay is decent and the benefits are great. You get ample paid time off along with sick leave. Also a number of paid holidays.
review.Cons: The hours can be long. Management is always completely unreasonable. Working outdoors in the elements year round is difficult. It is a very physical job.
review.Advice to management: Just use common sense and think for yourselves.

review.Pros: They care about their employees. Great place to work and great facilities to coach in. I've enjoyed my experience there thoroughly. They genuinely want the people working for them to be happy.
review.Cons: For me personally, the commute which I could change. A little of a pay cut coming from my previous county. A lot is expected of us, but pressure is a privelage.
review.Advice to management: No

review.Pros: The pros for me is that this is the same district I grew up going to school in so I know a lot of coworkers due to my history which makes it easier to connect to start new jobs within the district.
review.Cons: The budgeting within the district has fallen severely over the years which has led to so many problems including salary, security and students discipline to fall.

review.Pros: Great benefits. Good community. Exciting place to learn new techniques and meet new people to further ideas you might have. Good connections to go ahead.
review.Cons: Long hours. Pay could be a lot better. You do not go into academia for the paycheck. A lot of administrative layers to go through to get things done.
review.Advice to management: Know people in other departments

review.Pros: Good coworkers that will work with you and help you out anytime you need. Parents for the most part have been supportive and the kids have been mostly well behaved.
review.Cons: The biggest con is the micromanaging that is taking place now. Everyone needs to be on a very extreme schedule with no excuses for deviation. Administration focuses on what is going wrong regardless of how small vs. what is going right.
review.Advice to management: Let teachers teach

review.Pros: Pros of working at The University of Kansas Health System are there is a great benefits program, the Health System covers a fair amount of the premiums.  There is also a wonderful faculty of physicians that I would trust with a family member.  There are many job opportunities in my field so even if you're unhappy in one department, there could be a better fit for you elsewhere.
review.Cons: Cons are that even though they cover a fair amount of health insurance premiums, every year our premium costs increase, and our access to care decreases.  Access to care for all patients across the board is a struggle.  Also, since it is such a large organization with many levels of management, approvals for changes can take months, even years.  Even the tiniest adjustments are long drawn out processes, so much so that sometimes the problem has come and gone and there are even more downstream issues waiting for approval than if you were just able to adjust as you go or on the fly as you could in a smaller private institution, we could avoid a lot of headaches.

review.Pros: I can create my own hours. i am not obligated to be in the office by set hours. This makes my job a little less stressful.
review.Cons: The money. I am neither an hourly or salaried employee. I get paid per case. This is very stressful because I can go long periods without getting paid.

review.Pros: They have a great culture of promoting from within as well as providing educational  lopportunities for career advancement, they also have a very diverse Workforce
review.Cons: The only cons I can think of is there are very limited opportunities for remote or hybrid work schedules and a lot of the work requires either split shift or third shift hours which can be disruptive towards work-life balance

review.Pros: The pros of working at Somerset Independent Schools are the closeness of the staff, the family atmosphere, and the opportunities for advancement when on works hard.
review.Cons: The cons of working for Somerset Independent Schools are the impossibility of getting all required tasks completed within contract hours and the number of things required outside the scope of teaching.
review.Advice to management: Advice for management would be that smaller class sizes are imperative for higher test scores and teachers can only do so much within their contracted hours.

review.Pros: The company allows remote work, provides decent pay, good benefits, and there is a yearly bonus. Coworkers are generally ok. Work can be interesting at times.
review.Cons: Constant layoffs and instability, poor leadership, poor governance, inefficient processes, promotions based on favoritism, lack of career growth, culture fosters and rewards mediocrity and penalizes critical thinking.

review.Pros: gives me plenty of work experience, my coworker is easy to get along with, I've accumulated alot of vacation time, I just never use it
review.Cons: owner/operator lies alot and is a micromanager and takes everything we do for granted.  Gives us time to use but guilts us daily when we decide to use it

review.Pros: I earn a Decent pay and I work with great people and the work environment is very nice. There is a Starbucks on the campus.
review.Cons: There can be difficulties with the people I work with and its it very far away from home and takes a long time to get there.

review.Pros: Working at 988 provides me with a sense of real responsibility and gives me the opportunity to find purpose in meaningful work supporting others. It is also a job where there are significant opportunities for growth.
review.Cons: The cons of working at 988 is quick burnout due to the nature of the calls. There is also a medium-high turnover rate so you get to know people only for them to leave, which also leaves you taking on more work since they are gone until those positions are filled again.
review.Advice to management: Stop micromanaging. Everything was fine until this started. Being on camera enough all day with little to no privacy is already anxiety-provoking enough,

review.Pros: I make my own schedule, in addition to office work I get to extensively travel for work.  Last year I went to Milan, Italy and Dublin, Ireland.  They let me extend these work trips and travel around.  It is like I get paid to take a vacation!
review.Cons: Sometimes the clients can be a little aggressive, mean, and extremely unprepared.  You have to be very patient with clients and understand how busy they are which is why they are rarely prepared.
review.Advice to management: Better scheduling

review.Pros: I have a lot of flexibility with my schedule, the customer support is responsive, there are bonuses that I am eligible for, and the amount of money I make is great!
review.Cons: The customers can be disrespectful, same with the customer support at times. The traffic I face is not worth the money, and I burn a lot more gas on my car.
review.Advice to management: Listen to your employees more carefully.

review.Pros: I have minimum supervision, can get my quota done quickly and work prolific on the side, and my supervisors are kind and always support me.
review.Cons: I don't make enough money to survive without a lot of struggle. There are opportunities for advancement, but I was not chosen at the last interview.

review.Pros: Lots of opportunities for professional development and growth. There are multiple locations to work in the district. You are also considered a state employee when it comes to benefits.
review.Cons: There is a lot of reverse discrimination in the district. There are fewer opportunities for advancement if you are white rather than black. The district does not promote from within as much as they should.
review.Advice to management: They need to look at all employees and loyalty to the district

review.Pros: Decent salary and health benefits, co workers are nice, vacation time is ample. Work load is clear, union is good and dues are not too bad
review.Cons: Bosses are not competent in their expectations for work. Rollout of new policies are inefficient at best. Feedback and communication from management is never conise or constructive

review.Pros: Working closely within the others in my department means some good work friendship and camaraderie can develop.  We are given lots of flexibility with planning our own work and scheduling projects so we may do them how we please.  Management empowers us to problem solve and to enact our own solutions.
review.Cons: Small company culture is still present so often concerns are addressed by who voices them rather than their impact on the business.  Pay, vacation time, and total compensation also is stuck in a "small business" mindset rather than a large multinational firm.
review.Advice to management: Pay more for employees to stay, rather than pay the training costs associated with replacing them.

review.Pros: No dress code, lots of company contests, sales incentives, base pay plus commission, good hours, friendly work environment, free glasses once a year, nice 401k program.
review.Cons: My role is heavily dependent on sales, sometimes we don't have patients and the work doesn't feel as satisfying, higher than normal turnover rate at my location.
review.Advice to management: Treat the people who work for you like you want them to continue working for you.

review.Pros: The beneifts they provide are decent, ehich incudes healthcare, tuition reimbursment amongst others. The pay is competitve especially for entry level jobs. Peak season can really suck
review.Cons: The work conditions and what they ask out of you can sometimes be alot. As a driver the routes can really suck somedays and you have very little help

review.Pros: It offers great work-life balance, prioritizing people-focused values even while conscientiously focusing on providing fact-based policy analysis and unbiased research to our U.S. Congressional clients.
review.Cons: Being a federal government agency, we must adhere to arduous bureaucratic processes, intended to uphold key accountability principles but nevertheless rather soul sucking. There is also somewhat limited financial earnings trajectory as compared with similar roles in the private sector.
review.Advice to management: They should reconsider some required internal processes that may have the unintended consequence of delaying our response to key clients.

review.Pros: Working in education is great because you can help students learn and grow. It is very rewarding to see people succeed. Also you get good holidays and a steady schedule.
review.Cons: Working in Education can be hard because the pay is sometimes low. Teachers also have a lot of stress, heavy workloads, and many papers to grade after school hours.

review.Pros: I get to work from my house. I have healthcare through my company. It is a decent paying job and I enjoy what I do for work.
review.Cons: The technology that we use is not the most user friendly. My team of coworkers is not the greatest. We have lots of meetings to attend.

review.Pros: The benefits for the job are well-rounded and available in a timely manner. The company provides extensive onboarding and training for the area of knowledge you are working in.
review.Cons: The company is very large and that often contributes to delays and waiting times for requests to be processed and completed. No other major cons.

review.Pros: It is a big company with various different site locations so if I wanted to I could relocate to a different city within the company
review.Cons: It is a large company with hundreds of employees so it is easy to be underpaid and under-appreciated. They also do not have good benefits
review.Advice to management: Acknowledge the hard work of your employees more

review.Pros: I like working remotely. My hours are also flexible so I can easily work around my kids sports or sickness. I work with a small group of wonderful people too who are a pleasure to collaborate it.
review.Cons: There are times where they don't plan ahead appropriately so my plate can become overfilled some seasons with projects with unrealistic deadlines. Someone else's lack of planning becomes my headache.

review.Pros: The management at Critical Tool is very open to new ideas and listens fairly when you disagree with a decision. They pay well and offer excellent benefits and a very fair amount of vacation and PTO. The are very giving with any personal hardships and work with you.
review.Cons: They only let you carry over 3 days of PTO and if you don't use it you lose it. They aren't a communicative as I would like. Sometimes emails get unanswered because management is doing so much.
review.Advice to management: Have one on ones with each employee regularly (once a month) so you can get a feel of how they are doing. Not all employees will come to you if they are having a problem with something.

review.Pros: The pay is good for our area but not great given our workloads. I enjoy working with the majority of my coworkers. My supervisor is fair and easy to work for. He does not micro-manage his employees and I appreciate that about him
review.Cons: Working at a hospital is often very stressful and fast-paced work. You respond to many emergencies and must remain calm in very emotional circumstances. There are a lot of toxic environments in the hospital settings due to interpersonal issues and many instances of bullying that occur.
review.Advice to management: There is not much they can do. Bullying is somewhat expected and tolerated in that setting. It is well known that nurses "eat their young". they attitude is that it is a right of passage and you have to endure to survive and earn respect.

review.Pros: I like that I am getting experience in Project Management. I think that my skillset is really growing and I'm able to work independently but I also have a great team and mentor that I collaborate with.
review.Cons: The pay is just not that great. I feel that I'm am only getting by financially, and I have to supplement my income in other avenues.

review.Pros: I receive a pension when i retire, a nice salary, many holidays and every summer off. I get a good amount if sick time if I need it.
review.Cons: the clients can be demanding. administration can be difficult to deal with. more is asked of you every year with no raise. sometimes there are no breaks in a day

review.Pros: I am treated like a human being and not just a number or profit. My management actually cares about me and my overall well being.
review.Cons: I work a lot of hours and I am not paid for overtime. This use to be made for with generous raises but that is no longer the case.

review.Pros: The pay is good, the working conditions are good and we are union so we have a contract that is good for both  the workers and the administrators
review.Cons: Sometimes the admin forgets what it is like to work in the trenches.  They sometimes have unreasonable ideas and expectations of what goals can be accomplished

review.Pros: I can work remotely/hybrid. I work with celebrities. Boss is a good friend and he has been fun to work with as well as other staff
review.Cons: I do a lot of work and sometimes feel like i am underpaid for the type of work I do, and the owner can be harsh at times

review.Pros: the coworkers make the job great. I also have great benefits that make the job worth it. There is also job security, i don't have to worry about being fired easily.
review.Cons: The cons are working for the current administration, there are constant concerns of negative changes in the work force. there are also a lot of rules and regulations to follow.

review.Pros: Flexible work environment and people do their jobs. We do not have any weak links in the firm. I also like the work that I do and it is a very collaborative environment.
review.Cons: The rate of pay is a little lower than I would like at the moment. Also, sometimes it is too quiet in the office and I wish people would want to hang out and have a bit more fun.
review.Advice to management: A shared organization calendar with everyone's appointments and vacation time on it.

review.Pros: Flexibility for hours worked. Fully remote with no in-person requirements. Low standards if you just want a pay cheque but don't care about the dignity.
review.Cons: Your boss is a PDF. Almost all communication is one-way; we recently retired Slack in favour of GChat. No advancement opportunities. Projects start and stop with no warning and contractors are regularly left without work.
review.Advice to management: Consider a new career, preferably one where you lack managerial responsibilities.

review.Pros: The pros of working at Big Sky Self Storage are the fact that I get to interact with people.  I enjoy helping people out.  This job allows me to be my own boss.  I work for the owner directly, but I decide the schedule and how I get things done.
review.Cons: The cons to working at Big Sky Self Storage are that I live on site at the property.  I don't get a lot of time off.  I tend to have customers stop by or need help on my days off.

review.Pros: I have a consistent schedule.  I have weekends off, holidays off, and adequate vacation and sick time.  The pay is competitve and I enjoy all of my managers and coworkers.
review.Cons: The client we serve can be rather difficult sometimes, as you can never please everyone.  Management and higher-up corporate managers have constantly changing priorities and agendas, which makes works sometimes frustrating and confusing.
review.Advice to management: Don't be afraid to actually manage and stop avoiding (healthy) confrontation.

review.Pros: The workload is reasonable and the pay is higher than most similar jobs. Benefits are good and the schedule tends to be flexible. I have no issues requesting days off when I need to
review.Cons: You tend to be on the same area so work can get repetitive when doing it daily. The stores can get really busy so expect a lot of traffic.
review.Advice to management: Let people take their breaks as they want and not micromanage as often

review.Pros: Pay is pretty good in operations, because as a biotech manufacturing firm, profit margins are decent, and growth is steady. Benefits are nice. There is always something to learn about with the systems, and there is a ton of automation.
review.Cons: Responsibilities are highly dispersed and can be a bit ambiguous, as we are always expected to go the extra mile to own seemingly everything in the plant, whether we've been sufficiently trained on it or not. As with many companies, there is that sort of "sink or swim" vibe unless you've really been properly mentored and shown the ropes, so to speak. So you have to make sure you're a self-starter who can handle ambiguity, or else you can get overwhelmed quickly.
review.Advice to management: People could be disciplined more harshly, as most people are relatively replaceable at least in the professional sense. Nothing personal, as everyone has more depth than their corporate job demands from them, but a shake-up is often long overdue for managers who are scared to make moves and tend to let things slide.

review.Pros: It's full of people interested in doing their best. The leadership is kind and supportive. The overwhelming majority of our constituents are supportive and appreciative of our work.
review.Cons: It can be draining. The expectations are high which is good but challenging sometimes. Sometimes there is external pressure for excellence without meaningful conversation about of how that could or should happens.
review.Advice to management: None. My direct manager is positive and supportive. She facilitates me doing well at my job.

review.Pros: Small school district where everyone knows everyone and you get to learn about the people around you which is a lot more welcoming than a large district with 10+ buildings where administration is inaccessible and you feel like one of many and meet very few people.
review.Cons: Disorganization and lack of communication, taking advantage of employees to take on large roles without paying them for the additional work they're doing or paying them very little stipends for a fully salaried position.
review.Advice to management: Work on organizing time so it's easier to schedule office time and meetings

review.Pros: Embe is a large orginization that is able to give competitive pay for the industry that it exists within. It provides benefits including affordable health insurance. Additionally it is able to provide oppurtunities for growth and development and oppurtunities for consistent feedback.
review.Cons: The job is not easy and there is a lot of turnover. Training is left to employees who are expected to keep their regular job duties going as well as teach people the job. Being sick is treated negatively and sick policies are enforced inconsistently. Finally, the job is hard and support is inconsistent. Follow up does not always happen
review.Advice to management: To follow up, be understanding that people work to live and don't live to work, to be consistent in enforcing jobs and to provide consistent support when needed.

review.Pros: working at MK offers great growth opportunities , an exellent employee discount on luxury products , a stylish and fast-paced environment, and a highly collaborative team culture
review.Cons: common disadvantages include working long shifts on your feet , dealing with difficult customer behavior , strict sales goals , lower base compensation rtes , and challeges maintaining a healthy work -life balance during peak shopping seasons
review.Advice to management: make sure everything is runing smoothly

review.Pros: The biggest pro with working with the Georgia Dept of Community Supervision is the ability to be able to affect change in my community. It is a law enforcement agency and by our mission, we protect the citizens of Georgia. Also, I like the ability to work a hybrid schedule which includes remote working.
review.Cons: It is a state agency so our budget is fixed and determined by others. In other words, raises are hard to come by and will likely be by promotional opportunities.

review.Pros: For me, the pros have been that I actually feel respected within a company. I have a pharmacist who is respectful, and coworkers who are just as passionate about what they do. The company itself also has been incredible; I've had the pleasure of meeting almost all of our company's VPs
review.Cons: If I had to frame something as a con it would probably be the bit of chaos that ensued in our preopening weeks. That however is more so a state legal issue versus the company's fault.
review.Advice to management: Continue doing what you are doing

review.Pros: Company has a great work-life balance, and very professional for the size of the company. Lots of health insurance plan offering and benifits like 401k match.
review.Cons: Company has been pretty agressive with re-structuring but this has been more of a problem with contractors the FTEs. Its a niche industry thats hard to get into.

review.Pros: Areas gives a lot of flexibility to scheduling and has a relaxed work atmosphere. The people are generally helpful and courteous to workers and customers.
review.Cons: One of the biggest downsides to working at the company is there is a lot of disorganization and problems have to be solved on the fly.

review.Pros: Getting to teach students, good medical benefits, teacher perks, learning new things about teaching and students, the co-workers you get to work with, sometimies you have great parents
review.Cons: the pay sucks, the behavior issues in the classroom, getting beat up on by students, no support from the board of education, the lack of parenting, no support from parents, consistently changing curiculum or tools

review.Pros: The pros are the opportunities for promotions in management positions and a progressive work environment. The cons are the starting pay and less training while in a fast-paced environment.
review.Cons: Cons include very minimal training and how difficult it is to get employed here. It is also a job that requires a lot of labor and attention even if you work remotely the workload can burn you out.

review.Pros: Great service for both customers and employees, there are good benefits including theme park admission and health. I think the work in general is also not difficult.
review.Cons: The main con of working at this company is the low pay. The management is also negative as they sometimes do not have clear direction and can micromanage a little.
review.Advice to management: Trust your employees more, make clear decisions, and communicate.

review.Pros: the pros are getting to meet so many new people everyday, having fun while working, being around good friends, and making good money.  the only cons would be the late nights and dealing with drunk people.
review.Cons: the late nights working until 4 or 5 in the morning and having to deal with drunk and intoxicated people every night of the week
review.Advice to management: none

review.Pros: The Pros are being able to work from home and make your own schedule, semi reasonable pay and paid training. The jobs are pretty easy and you are able to choose what job you would like to work.
review.Cons: The Cons are that some of the jobs are low pay and only pay by the actual talk minute and sometime you can be waiting almost an hour for a call to come in which lowers your pay. I am not a fan of their pay system, sometimes it take all day to get your direct deposit.
review.Advice to management: More accountability for mistakes by your management team. I have ran into several issues such as hours being taken away with no explanation and having to wait for someone to respond to me about what happened

review.Pros: I get to interact with alot of different people throuhout the day as I serve them. That lights up my day because i like serving people
review.Cons: one of the major issues ive experienced so far is dealing with difficult customers or even having to deal with shoplifters. it makes me keep thinking alot

review.Pros: The culture is very strong here and everyone is extremely professional and good at what they do. The benefits are on par with similar organizations.
review.Cons: Timelines in marketing can be a bit crazy and often experience last minute changes. Quick pivots are necessary but typically work out in the end.

review.Pros: Working as a driver and logistics operator offers steady employment, competitive pay, and strong job stability. Key benefits nclude modern facilities, supportove team disptachers and dependable scheduling
review.Cons: Demanding shift bhours, strict delivery deadlines, and long periods away from home. Unpredicatble traffic delays, physical fatigue, and occassional communication gaps between dispatchers and drivers
review.Advice to management: Management should working on the communciation gap between dispatchers and drivers which causes work stress

review.Pros: There's a lot of flexibility when it comes to working hybrid. Although there's a mandated four days in office, most come in two or three times a week without hassle. There's also the ability to leave early or come late as needed. Benefits are a huge plus. Decent time off coupled with a separate pool for sick leave and a third, smaller pool for other. There's a full days worth of paid volunteer off on top of a pre-scheduled day once a year when offices shut down to volunteer. If you're looking at becoming a parent, great parental benefits and leave.
review.Cons: Lack of growth opportunities. Like any marketing company it's a fight to try and get a decent raise without leaving and coming back. There's lack of transparency on how to get promoted as well which make it difficult to know how one is doing. You also can't argue for what percentage increase you want or promotion, you simply have to accept it. Not to mention the cycles are twice a year so good luck fighting with people for the raise/promotion money during your allotted cycle (summer or winter).
review.Advice to management: Transparency on how to get promotions would be beneficial. There doesn't appear to be a set check list and it's at the whims of the department lead. There also appears to be a lack of communication when big shifts happen at VML. Not sure if this is a larger issue of VML leadership not telling department leads the information or what, but this has been creating frustration and gaps in employee knowledge.

review.Pros: Great pay, flexible hours, retirement benefits. Great supervisors who are always willing to help. My co-workers who answer any question and check on me periodically.
